#### Étale cohomology agrees with pro-étale cohomology of ν^*F, and ν^* commutes with qcqs direct images

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-etale-comparison` · theorem · packet H0

Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and ν: X_proét → X_ét the projection (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu). (i) For every abelian sheaf (or sheaf of Λ-modules) F on X_ét the unit F → Rν_*ν^*F is an isomorphism in D⁺(X_ét); hence H^i(X_ét, F) ≅ H^i(X_proét, ν^*F) for all i and ν^*: D⁺(X_ét, Λ) → D⁺(X_proét, Λ) is fully faithful. (ii) For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism f: X → Y of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces and F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ), the base-change morphism ν_Y^* Rf_ét,* F → Rf_proét,* ν_X^* F is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- X, Y locally noetherian analytic; f quasi-compact and quasi-separated in (ii).
- F a sheaf of abelian groups or Λ-modules on the étale site (not an arbitrary pro-étale sheaf).

**Proof.**

1. (i) R^iν_*ν^*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^i(U, ν^*F) with U ∈ X_ét regarded in X_proét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification). For i = 0 this is F by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/nu-pullback-sections-qcqs. For i > 0 and U qcqs, H^i(U, ν^*F) = H^i(U, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity with a constant presentation), and every class in H^i(U, F) vanishes étale-locally on U, so the sheafification is zero.
2. Full faithfulness on D⁺: Hom(ν^*K, ν^*L) = Hom(K, Rν_*ν^*L) = Hom(K, L) by adjunction and (i) applied to the cohomology sheaves of L (way-out argument on bounded below complexes).
3. (ii) Both sides have i-th cohomology sheaf equal to the sheafification of the presheaf sending a qcqs U = lim U_j → Y in Y_proét to colim_j H^i(U_j ×_Y X, F): the left side by (i) for Y and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification for f_ét, the right side by the same lemma for f_proét and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity applied to U ×_Y X = lim U_j ×_Y X (qcqs because f is qcqs).

**Acceptance.**

- H^i(X_ét, ℤ/p) = H^i(X_proét, ℤ/p) for every locally noetherian analytic X (used in Scholze's primitive comparison theorem).
- Non-example for (ii) without quasi-compactness: for the non-quasi-compact boundary complement j: U → X of a smooth pair, the comparison of ν^*Rj_ét,* and Rj_proét,*ν^* is not asserted (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/boundary-complement-restriction).

### Affinoid-local descriptions

Restriction to the affinoid étale basis is an equivalence of sheaf categories and of D⁺, compatible with sections; vector bundles on strongly sheafy affinoids are étale acyclic.

#### Affinoid-local description of étale sheaves, their cohomology and derived direct images

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description` · theorem · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, Λ a ring and X_ét^aff the stable affinoid étale basis (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison). (i) Restriction to X_ét^aff is an equivalence Sh(X_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff, Λ), exact in both directions, inducing D⁺(X_ét, Λ) ≃ D⁺(X_ét^aff, Λ) compatible with RΓ(U, −) for U ∈ X_ét^aff; a presheaf on X_ét^aff is a sheaf iff it is a sheaf for rational coverings and satisfies descent for single faithfully finite étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction). (ii) For X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, X_ét^aff is equivalent to the opposite of the category of complete Huber pairs reached from (A, A⁺) by finite chains of rational localisations and finite étale extensions, so an étale sheaf on X is a functor on such A-algebras with these two descent conditions. (iii) Étale-locality on the target: for g: X′ → X and v: V → X in X_ét with g_V: X′ ×_X V → V, restriction commutes with derived direct image, (Rg_*K)|_V ≅ R(g_V)_*(K|_{X′ ×_X V}) for K ∈ D⁺(X′_ét, Λ); in particular R^q g_*F can be computed over any open affinoid cover of X. (iv) For U ∈ X_ét quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^n(U, F) is the Čech cohomology of any finite covering of U by basis objects on whose finite intersections F is acyclic (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison), and H^n(U, −) commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites, the étale topos of a qcqs X being coherent with generating family X_ét^aff).

**Hypotheses.**

- X locally strongly sheafy analytic; in (iv) U quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
- K bounded below in (iii).

**Proof.**

1. (i) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (c) (dense subsite, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv); an equivalence of abelian categories preserves injectives, so derived functors correspond; the sheaf criterion is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction.
2. (ii) Objects of X_ét^aff over X = Spa(A, A⁺) are the chains of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison, with morphisms the X-morphisms of adic spaces, which on affinoids are maps of complete Huber pairs over (A, A⁺) (anchor Layer 5 morphisms from affinoids; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) for the finite étale steps).
3. (iii) For W ∈ V_ét, ((g_*F)|_V)(W) = F(W ×_X X′) = F(W ×_V (X′ ×_X V)) = ((g_V)_*(F|_{X′ ×_X V}))(W), so restriction commutes with g_* on sheaves; restriction preserves injectives (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives), hence commutes with the derived functors.
4. (iv) Leray acyclicity (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (a)); a qcqs U has a finite covering by basis objects with basis finite intersections (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (b)); coherence of the étale topos of a qcqs space from the qcqs generating family X_ét^aff (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos) and then DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(K, O_K) (rank-one plus ring), (ii) identifies Sh(X_ét, Λ) with sheaves on the opposite of finite étale K-algebras, i.e. discrete Galois modules.
- For an open affinoid cover X = V₁ ∪ V₂ with V₁ ∩ V₂ affinoid, (iii)–(iv) give the Mayer–Vietoris sequence ⋯ → H^n(X, F) → H^n(V₁, F) ⊕ H^n(V₂, F) → H^n(V₁ ∩ V₂, F) → ⋯ (compare Mathlib's Mayer–Vietoris sequence for Sheaf.H).

#### Étale acyclicity of vector bundles on strongly sheafy affinoids

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles` · theorem · packet H0

Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly sheafy Tate ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair) and M a finite projective A-module. Let M̃_ét be the presheaf on X_ét^aff sending Y = Spa(B, B⁺) to M ⊗_A B. Then M̃_ét is a sheaf on X_ét (via AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison) and H^i(Y_ét, M̃_ét) = 0 for every Y ∈ X_ét^aff and i > 0; in particular H^i(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) = 0 for i > 0 and H^0(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) = A. Consequently, on a locally strongly sheafy analytic X, for a vector bundle E on X_an the pullback λ^*E to X_ét satisfies Rλ_*λ^*E = E for λ: X_ét → X_an, and vector bundles on X_an and on X_ét correspond (Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22 (d)). This is a statement about O-modules; it implies nothing about constant coefficients: H^1(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)_ét, ℤ/p) ≠ 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- A complete strongly sheafy Tate ring (so every object of X_ét^aff is a sheafy affinoid); M finite projective.
- The coefficient sheaf is M ⊗_A O, not a constant or torsion sheaf.

**Proof.**

1. Rational coverings: for Y ∈ X_ét^aff (strongly sheafy by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (b)), the Čech complex of M ⊗_A B on every rational covering is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity; Kedlaya–Liu 2.4.23).
2. Faithfully finite étale maps: for a surjective finite étale Spa(B′) → Spa(B), B → B′ is faithfully flat (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d)), so the Amitsur complex N ⊗_B B′^{⊗(•+1)} of N = M ⊗_A B is exact (Stacks Tag 023M); the fibre products are Spa(B′ ⊗_B ⋯ ⊗_B B′) with the uncompleted tensor products (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).
3. These two cases imply universal Čech acyclicity on X_ét^aff (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction; Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.20), hence M̃_ét is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology on basis objects (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (b); Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.21).
4. For λ: X_ét → X_an: R^qλ_*λ^*E is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(U_ét, λ^*E) on opens (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification), which vanishes on affinoid U for q > 0 by the above and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/vector-bundle-global-generation; the equivalence of vector bundles then follows from descent of finite projective modules along finite étale covers (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent).
5. Non-example: H^1(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)_ét, ℤ/p) = H^1(Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), ℤ/p) ≠ 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image, Galois test).

**Acceptance.**

- Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22 (c): for Y ∈ X_ét^aff, H^i(Y, M̃) = M̃(Y) for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0.
- For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and M = A: H^1(X_ét, O) = 0 while H^1(X_ét, ℤ/p) ≠ 0.

### Subsets, geometric stalks and supports

The pseudo-adic site of a subset, the stalks of étale sheaves on the spectrum of a geometric field pair (global sections are the stalk at the closed point and higher cohomology vanishes, for C⁺ of any rank), extension by zero, restriction to closed and locally closed subsets with cohomology with supports and the localisation sequence, and the comparison of ordinary Ext and D⁺ cohomology with E1's enhanced derived category.

#### The étale site of a subset of an analytic adic space (pseudo-adic étale site)

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site` · construction · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and S ⊆ |X| a subset. The étale site of (X, S) is (X, S)_ét := (X_ét, J_S): the category X_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site with the Grothendieck topology J_S in which a sieve R on u: U → X is covering iff u^{-1}(S) ⊆ ⋃_{(f: V → U) ∈ R} f(|V|); equivalently, it is generated by the families (f_i: U_i → U) with u^{-1}(S) ⊆ ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|). Properties: (i) every covering of X_ét is a J_S-covering, and the identity functor is continuous and finite-limit preserving, giving a morphism of sites i_S: (X, S)_ét → X_ét with i_{S,*} the inclusion of J_S-sheaves and i_S^{-1} = J_S-sheafification, exact; (ii) for a geometric point ξ of X whose support lies in S, the fibre functor of ξ is a point of (X, S)_ét, these points form a conservative family, and (i_S^{-1}F)_ξ = F_ξ; (iii) S = |X| gives X_ét, S = ∅ gives the trivial topos (every sheaf is terminal), and for S = |W| with W ⊆ X an open subspace, (X, S)_ét and W_ét have equivalent sheaf categories via restriction; (iv) a morphism g: X′ → X and S′ ⊆ g^{-1}(S) give a morphism of sites (X′, S′)_ét → (X, S)_ét by base change; (v) T ⊆ S gives i_{T,S}: (X, T)_ét → (X, S)_ét with i_T = i_S ∘ i_{T,S}. When S is convex (closed under the specialisations lying between two of its points) and locally pro-constructible — tested on spectral open neighbourhoods of the points of S, the convention also used by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/pairs-and-pseudo-adic-supports, under which locally closed subsets of locally spectral spaces qualify — (X, S) is a pseudo-adic space in Huber's sense; for S closed or locally closed and constructible this holds, and (X, S) is in general not an adic space.

**Hypotheses.**

- X locally strongly sheafy analytic; S an arbitrary subset of |X| for the construction, convex and locally pro-constructible for Huber's pseudo-adic conditions.
- The site is a Grothendieck topology on the category X_ét itself; no adic space structure on S is asserted.

**Construction.**

1. Topology: J_S is a Grothendieck topology (stability under pullback uses that the preimage of S under a composite is the preimage of the preimage and that the image of |V ×_U U′| → |U′| contains the preimage of the image, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; transitivity is union of images); it contains J because a jointly surjective family covers every subset.
2. (i) The identity X_ét → X_ét sends J-covers to J_S-covers and preserves finite limits (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback; exactness as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules).
3. (ii) Points: for ξ with support s ∈ S, a lift ū of ξ to U maps the closed point to a point of u^{-1}(S); a J_S-covering family covers it, the pullback of the family to Spa(C, C⁺) contains a member whose image contains the closed point, and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (iii) gives a section, hence a lift (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point). Conservativity: a sieve through which every lift of every such ξ factors covers u^{-1}(S), by the proof of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points restricted to points of S.
4. (iii) S = ∅: the empty sieve covers every object. S = |W|: the sieve of U generated by U ×_X W → U is J_S-covering, so a J_S-sheaf is determined by its values on objects over W, and those form W_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site).
5. (iv), (v): base change preserves the covering condition because preimages of S′ ⊆ g^{-1}(S) map into preimages of S.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite` (structure): The site (X_ét, J_S) attached to X and S ⊆ |X|.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.topology` (data): The Grothendieck topology J_S on X_ét.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.mem_topology_iff` (characterisation): A sieve R on U is J_S-covering iff u^{-1}(S) ⊆ ⋃_{f ∈ R} f(|V|).
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.le_topology` (relation): smallEtaleTopology X ≤ J_S.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.incl` (functoriality): i_S^{-1} (J_S-sheafification, exact) ⊣ i_{S,*} (inclusion of J_S-sheaves).
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.point` (constructor): The point of (X, S)_ét attached to a geometric point with support in S.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.isConservativeFamily` (characterisation): Geometric points with support in S form a conservative family of points.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.stalk_incl` (simp): (i_S^{-1}F)_ξ = F_ξ for ξ supported in S.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.equivOpen` (equivalence): Sh((X, |W|)_ét) ≃ Sh(W_ét) for an open subspace W.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.map` (functoriality): The morphism of sites (X′, S′)_ét → (X, S)_ét for g: X′ → X with S′ ⊆ g^{-1}(S), with map_comp.
- `AdicSpace.PseudoAdicSite.IsPseudoAdic` (other): Huber's conditions on S: convex and locally pro-constructible; satisfied by locally closed constructible S.

**Unit tests.**

- `PseudoAdicSite.test_univ` (degenerate): For S = |X|, (X, S)_ét = X_ét and i_S is the identity; for S = ∅ every sheaf on (X, S)_ét is a terminal object.
- `PseudoAdicSite.test_open` (compatibility): For S = |W| with W ⊆ X open, restriction gives Sh((X, S)_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(W_ét, Λ), compatibly with i_S^{-1} and W → X.
- `PseudoAdicSite.test_closed_point` (computation): For X = Spa(C, C⁺) (C algebraically closed, C⁺ of rank 2) and S the closed point, F ↦ F_s is an equivalence Sh((X, S)_ét, Λ) ≃ Mod_Λ.
- `PseudoAdicSite.test_not_adic` (non-example): For the closed unit disc X over K and Z = X ∖ {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} (ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of K), Z is closed, infinite and not open (the disc is connected), so it is the underlying set of no open adic subspace and of no Zariski-closed adic subspace; i_Z^{-1} is not restriction to an adic subspace.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed and C⁺ of rank 2, and S = {s} the closed point, Sh((X, S)_ét, Λ) is equivalent to Λ-modules via the stalk at s.

#### Étale sheaves on Spa(C, C⁺): global sections are the stalk at the closed point and higher cohomology vanishes

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/geometric-stalks-at-field-pairs` · theorem · packet H0

Let C be an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of any rank r ≥ 1, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with closed point s, and Λ a ring. (a) For every F ∈ Sh(S_ét, Λ), Γ(S, F) = F_{id} is the stalk at the geometric point id_S (support s); Γ(S, −) is exact and commutes with all colimits. (b) H^n(S, F) = 0 for all n > 0 and all F. (c) Every étale map V → S is a local isomorphism, so restriction to the opens of |S| is an equivalence Sh(S_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(|S|, Λ); |S| is the chain, under specialisation, of the valuation rings V with C⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ O_C (r of them when r is finite), and the stalk at the point V corresponds to the geometric point Spa(C, V) → S. (d) For a locally strongly sheafy analytic X and a geometric point ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X, F_ξ ≅ Γ(Spa(C, C⁺), ξ^{-1}F), naturally in F. (e) Higher rank is retained: for r ≥ 2 the family of stalks at the rank-one points of all such S does not detect nonzero sheaves (the skyscraper at s), and Γ(S, F) is the stalk at the closed point, not at the rank-one point Spa(C, O_C).

**Hypotheses.**

- C algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean, nontrivially valued; C⁺ open, bounded, a valuation ring of any rank.
- For K not algebraically closed the statement fails (Galois cohomology).

**Proof.**

1. (a) The category N(id) of étale neighbourhoods of the geometric point id_S has the initial object (S, id): a neighbourhood (U, ū) receives the unique morphism ū from (S, id) (ū is an S-morphism S → U lifting id). Hence the stalk colimit is F(S) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (c)), and stalks are exact and commute with colimits (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi)).
2. (b) Γ(S, −) is exact, so its right derived functors vanish in positive degrees (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image).
3. (c) Locally on the source an étale V → S is an open subspace of a finite étale W → S′ over an open S′ ⊆ S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism). The rational subsets of S are the Spa(C, V′) for overrings V′ ⊇ C⁺ generated by one element (field pairs with C algebraically closed) and cover S′; over each of them W splits as a finite disjoint union of copies (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (ii)). Hence W → S′, and so V → S, is a local isomorphism, and sheaves on the site of local isomorphisms over |S| are sheaves on |S| (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i) for the description of |S|).
4. (d) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (d): (ξ^{-1}F)_{id} ≅ F_{ξ ∘ id} = F_ξ, combined with (a).
5. (e) The skyscraper i_{s,*}Λ (via (c): the sheaf on |S| with sections Λ on S and 0 on S ∖ {s}) has stalk Λ at s and 0 at every other point.

**Acceptance.**

- H^n(Spa(C, C⁺), Λ) = 0 for n > 0 and H^0 = Λ.
- Non-example: for K a complete nonarchimedean field that is not algebraically closed, H^1(Spa(K, O_K), ℤ/ℓ) = H^1(Gal(K^sep/K), ℤ/ℓ) ≠ 0 for suitable ℓ (for example K = ℚ_p, ℓ = p), and Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) is a nonsplit finite étale cover for every nontrivial finite separable extension L (L⁺ the integral closure of K⁺).

Every fibre functor of the topos X~_et is isomorphic to a fibre functor of the form ε_ξ.” — Huber's fibre functors ε_ξ at geometric points, computed here as global sections over Spa(C, C⁺).

#### Extension by zero, restriction to closed and locally closed subsets, and cohomology with supports

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero` · construction · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring. (i) For u: U → X in X_ét, extension by zero u_!: Sh(U_ét, Λ) → Sh(X_ét, Λ) is the left adjoint of the restriction u^{-1} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (a)); it is exact, (u_!G)_ξ = ⊕_{ū} G_ū over the lifts ū of the geometric point ξ to U, and u_! ≅ u_* when u is finite étale. (ii) For an open subspace j: U ⊆ X with closed complement Z = |X| ∖ |U|, let i: (X, Z)_ét → X_ét be the pseudo-adic site of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site; then j_!, j^{-1}, j_*, i^{-1}, i_* satisfy j^{-1}j_! ≅ id ≅ j^{-1}j_*, i^{-1}i_* ≅ id, j^{-1}i_* = 0, i^{-1}j_! = 0, and i_* is exact. (iii) Sections with support: ℋ_Z(F) := ker(F → j_*j^{-1}F), Γ_Z(X, F) := ker(F(X) → F(U)), i^!F := i^{-1}ℋ_Z(F) (right adjoint of i_*), with derived functors RΓ_Z(X, −), Ri^! on D⁺ and H^n_Z(X, F) := H^n RΓ_Z(X, F). (iv) For a locally closed T = U′ ∩ Z′ (U′ open, Z′ closed), extension by zero from T: i_{T,!} := j_{U′,!} ∘ (i_{Z′∩U′ ⊆ U′})_*, exact and independent of the presentation of T. No closed or locally closed subset is replaced by an adic subspace: (X, Z) is a pseudo-adic space, not an adic space.

**Hypotheses.**

- X locally strongly sheafy analytic; U open (for (ii)–(iii)) or étale over X (for (i)).
- Λ an arbitrary ring.

**Construction.**

1. (i) u_! is mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback along Over.forget U with values in ModuleCat Λ (left Kan extension and sheafification), under U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site); the stalk formula follows from the description of stalks as colimits over neighbourhoods and the cofinality of neighbourhoods of the lifts; exactness from the stalk formula and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi). For finite étale u, the natural map u_! → u_* is an isomorphism: the question is étale-local on X, and étale-locally a finite étale u is a finite disjoint union of copies of the base (induction on the locally constant degree, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d), splitting off the open and closed diagonal of U ×_X U → U, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), where both functors are the finite direct sum.
2. (ii) Stalks at geometric points with support in U, resp. in Z (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence (b)); i_* exact because i_*G is computed on the same category X_ét and its stalks at points in U vanish while those in Z are stalks of G.
3. (iii) ℋ_Z is left exact as a kernel; i^! is right adjoint to i_* because a map i_*G → F factors through ℋ_Z(F) (its restriction to U vanishes); derived functors by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image (enough injectives).
4. (iv) Independence of the presentation: two presentations have a common refinement U″ = U′ ∩ U‴ in which T is closed, and extension by zero along open immersions composes (j_{U″,!} = j_{U′,!} ∘ (U″ ⊆ U′)_!).

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.extendByZero` (constructor): u_!: Sh(U_ét, Λ) ⥤ Sh(X_ét, Λ) for u: U → X étale.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.extendByZeroAdj` (universal-property): u_! ⊣ u^{-1}.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.extendByZero_exact` (instance): u_! preserves finite limits and colimits.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.stalk_extendByZero` (simp): (u_!G)_ξ ≅ ⊕_{lifts ū of ξ} G_ū; for an open immersion, G_ξ or 0 according as supp ξ ∈ U.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.extendByZero_iso_pushforward_of_finiteEtale` (compatibility): u_! ≅ u_* for u finite étale.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.restrict_extendByZero` (simp): j^{-1}j_! ≅ id for an open immersion j.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.closedRestrict` (constructor): i^{-1}: Sh(X_ét, Λ) ⥤ Sh((X, Z)_ét, Λ) and i_*, for the closed complement Z of an open U.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.sectionsWithSupport` (constructor): ℋ_Z(F) = ker(F → j_*j^{-1}F), Γ_Z(X, F), and i^! = i^{-1}ℋ_Z with i_* ⊣ i^!.
- `AdicSpace.cohomologyWithSupport` (constructor): H^n_Z(X, F) := H^n(RΓ_Z(X, F)), RΓ_Z the right derived functor of Γ_Z on D⁺.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.extendByZeroLocallyClosed` (constructor): i_{T,!} for T = U′ ∩ Z′ locally closed, independent of the presentation.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.closedRestrict_extendByZero` (simp): i^{-1}j_! = 0 and j^{-1}i_* = 0.

**Unit tests.**

- `extendByZero_test_disc` (computation): For the quasi-compact open j: U = {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), Γ(X, j_!Λ) = 0 and Γ(X, j_*Λ) ≅ Λ.
- `extendByZero_test_univ` (degenerate): For j = id_X, j_! = id and Z = ∅; for U = ∅, j_! = 0 and i_* i^{-1} = id.
- `extendByZero_test_sheafPullback` (compatibility): u_! is naturally isomorphic to Functor.sheafPullback (Over.forget U) with values in ModuleCat Λ under U_ét ≃ X_ét/U, and agrees with the j_! of AdicSpacesPartII:R4/boundary-complement-restriction for the boundary complement of a smooth pair.
- `extendByZero_test_stalk_boundary` (non-example): For U = {|T| ≤ |p|} in the closed disc over ℚ_p and the rank-two point x ∉ U in the closure of U (a specialisation of the Gauss point of radius |p|), (j_!Λ)_x = 0 but (j_*Λ)_x ≅ Λ, so j_! ≠ j_* although U is quasi-compact.
- `extendByZero_test_adjunction` (characterisation): For an open immersion j: U ⊆ X, the natural map j_!G → j_*G is a monomorphism, and a section s ∈ (j_*G)(V) = G(V ×_X U) lies in (j_!G)(V) iff its support is closed in |V|; i^! is right adjoint to i_*.

**Acceptance.**

- For the quasi-compact open j: U = {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ X = closed unit disc over ℚ_p: Γ(X, j_!Λ) = 0 while Γ(X, j_*Λ) = Λ, and j_!Λ is constructible in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves.
- For U = X: j_! = id, Z = ∅ and i^{-1}F = 0.

#### Ordinary Ext and D⁺ cohomology agree with the shared enhanced derived category

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/ordinary-vs-enhanced-ext-comparison` · comparison · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring; let D(X_ét, Λ) = `DerivedCategory (Sh(X_ét, Λ))`, D⁺(X_ét, Λ) ⊆ D(X_ét, Λ) the full subcategory of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image, and 𝒟(X_ét, Λ) the enhanced derived category of E1 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category), whose homotopy category is D(X_ét, Λ). Then: (a) for F, G ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) and n ≥ 0, Ext^n(F, G) (Mathlib `Abelian.Ext`) ≅ Hom_{D(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]) ≅ Hom_{D⁺(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]) ≅ π_0 Map_{𝒟(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]); in particular H^n(U, G) ≅ π_0 Map_𝒟(j_{U!}Λ, G[n]) for U ∈ X_ét, with j_{U!}Λ the extension by zero of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero; (b) a bounded below complex of injective sheaves is K-injective, so for K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) the value RΓ(U, K) of the D⁺ right derived functor agrees with E1's enhanced RΓ(U, K) computed by K-injective replacement (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements), and likewise Rg_*K and Rν_*K; (c) the comparisons in (a)–(b) are compatible with composition (Yoneda product), with the connecting maps of long exact sequences and with g^{-1}. Consequently every classical statement of H0–H5 formulated in D⁺ is a statement about E1's enhanced objects restricted to bounded-below complexes, and conversely.

**Hypotheses.**

- Λ an arbitrary ring; the enhanced category is E1's for the ringed site (X_ét, Λ_X).
- Only bounded-below complexes are claimed to be computed by injective resolutions.

**Proof.**

1. (a) First two isomorphisms: definition of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext as shifted Hom between single complexes in the localisation at quasi-isomorphisms, and full faithfulness of DerivedCategory.Plus ⊆ DerivedCategory (mathlib:DerivedCategory.Plus is a full subcategory). Third: E1's comparison of the homotopy category of 𝒟(X_ét, Λ) with mathlib:DerivedCategory (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category), under which π_0 of mapping spaces is Hom in the homotopy category. The U-version uses Hom(j_{U!}Λ, −) = Γ(U, −).
2. (b) mathlib:CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective: bounded below complexes of injectives are K-injective; so an injective resolution is a K-injective replacement, and E1's functorial replacement is homotopy equivalent to it (a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes is a homotopy equivalence, mathlib:CochainComplex.IsKInjective.quasiIso_iff); applying Γ(U, −) (resp. g_*, ν_*) to homotopy-equivalent complexes gives isomorphic objects.
3. (c) Both sides are computed by the same K-injective complexes, and Yoneda composition, connecting maps and pullback are induced by maps of complexes.

**Acceptance.**

- For U = X and G = Λ_X: H^n(X, Λ) ≅ π_0 Map_𝒟(Λ_X, Λ_X[n]).
- The comparison is required for the passage from Huber's D⁺ statements (H1–H3) to ECD's unbounded D_ét on the diamond side.

#### Stalks of j_! and i_*, the localisation sequence and the long exact sequence of cohomology with supports

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence` · lemma · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, j: U ⊆ X an open subspace with closed complement Z and i: (X, Z)_ét → X_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero). (a) For a geometric point ξ of X with support x: (j_!G)_ξ = G_ξ if x ∈ U and 0 if x ∈ Z; (i_*H)_ξ = H_ξ if x ∈ Z and 0 if x ∈ U. (b) For F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) the sequence 0 → j_!j^{-1}F → F → i_*i^{-1}F → 0 is exact. (c) For K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) there are distinguished triangles j_!j^{-1}K → K → i_*i^{-1}K → and i_*Ri^!K → K → Rj_*j^{-1}K →, and a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^n_Z(X, K) → H^n(X, K) → H^n(U, K) → H^{n+1}_Z(X, K) → ⋯, natural in K. (d) For an injective sheaf I, Γ(X, I) → Γ(U, I) is surjective.

**Hypotheses.**

- U open, Z its closed complement; supports of geometric points are points of |X|.

**Proof.**

1. (a) A geometric point with support in U has a neighbourhood basis of étale objects over U, on which j_!G = G; with support in Z, every lift to an object over U is impossible (the closed point would map into U), so the colimit defining (j_!G)_ξ is over sections of the Kan extension that vanish; for i_*: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site (ii) and the vanishing of J_Z-sheaves on objects over U (the empty sieve covers them).
2. (b) Exactness is checked on stalks at all geometric points (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi)) using (a).
3. (d) Γ(X, −) = Hom(Λ_X, −), Γ(U, −) = Hom(j_!Λ_U, −) and j_!Λ_U → Λ_X is a monomorphism by (a); Hom(−, I) is exact.
4. (c) Apply (b) to an injective resolution, use (d) to get the short exact sequence of complexes 0 → Γ_Z(X, I^•) → Γ(X, I^•) → Γ(U, I^•) → 0, and take cohomology (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image); the second triangle is the derived form of 0 → i_*i^!I → I → j_*j^{-1}I → 0 for injective I.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ of rank 2, U = the generic point and Z = the closed point: H^0_Z(X, Λ) = 0, H^1_Z(X, Λ) = 0, since H^n(X, Λ) → H^n(U, Λ) is an isomorphism (both spaces have trivial étale cohomology in positive degrees and Γ = Λ).
- The Berkovich analogue: Berkovich Proposition 5.2.6 (ii) and Corollary 5.2.7.

### Local systems, constructible sheaves and Tate twists

Locally constant sheaves and torsion local systems, their equivalence with finite étale covers; Huber's constructible sheaves, defined by finite partitions into constructible locally closed subsets on which the restriction to the pseudo-adic site is locally constant of finite type, with their stability properties; every sheaf as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves (though not of its constructible subsheaves: the H0 review's counterexample on the closed disc is a test of the node); the Kummer sequence and Tate twists.

#### Locally constant sheaves and torsion local systems on the étale site

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems` · definition · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring. A sheaf F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is locally constant if there are an étale covering (U_α → X)_α and Λ-modules M_α with F|_{U_α} ≅ (M_α)_{U_α}; it is locally constant of finite type if the M_α can be chosen finitely generated. A torsion local system of rank r is a locally constant sheaf of Λ-modules for a ring Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n ≥ 1 whose local values M_α are free of rank r (for Λ noetherian, a locally constant sheaf of finite type with finite projective values is called lisse). For ℓ a prime, a lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaf is an inverse system (L_m)_{m ≥ 1} with L_m a locally constant sheaf of finitely generated ℤ/ℓ^m-modules, such that the system is isomorphic in the pro-category to one with L_{m+1}/ℓ^m ≅ L_m; on X_proét (X locally noetherian) a lisse Ẑ_ℓ-sheaf is a sheaf of Ẑ_ℓ-modules locally isomorphic to Ẑ_ℓ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} M with M finitely generated, Ẑ_ℓ := lim_m ν^*(ℤ/ℓ^m). The same definitions apply on the pseudo-adic sites (X, S)_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site).

**Hypotheses.**

- X locally strongly sheafy analytic (locally noetherian for the pro-étale clause).
- Coverings are A1's étale coverings; the local trivialising cover is part of the existence statement, not data.

**Construction.**

1. Definition by the existence of a trivialising covering; the pro-category condition for lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves follows Scholze's Definition 8.1.
2. Closure properties (API): pullback preserves local constancy (g^{-1} commutes with restriction and sends constant sheaves to constant sheaves, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules); kernels, cokernels, extensions, ⊗ and Hom of locally constant sheaves of finite type over a noetherian Λ are locally constant of finite type (a map of constant sheaves on a connected object is constant, and extensions split étale-locally over a common refinement), as Berkovich records for finite locally constant sheaves in any topos.
3. Equivalence with finite étale covers and π₁-modules: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant` (structure): F is locally constant: there is an étale covering on whose members F is constant.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.ofFiniteType` (structure): Local values finitely generated Λ-modules.
- `AdicSpace.TorsionLocalSystem` (structure): The full subcategory of locally constant sheaves with local values free of finite rank, for Λ with nΛ = 0.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.isLocallyConstant_const` (example): Constant sheaves M_X are locally constant.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.pullback` (functoriality): g^{-1} preserves local constancy (and finite type, and rank).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction to U ∈ X_ét and to pseudo-adic sites preserves local constancy.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.kernel` (other): Kernels, cokernels and extensions of locally constant sheaves of finite type over noetherian Λ are locally constant of finite type.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.tensor` (other): F ⊗_Λ G and Hom_Λ(F, G) are locally constant of finite type.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.stalk_iso` (relation): On connected X all stalks of a locally constant sheaf are isomorphic (specialisation maps are isomorphisms).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.equivFiniteEtale` (equivalence): Locally constant sheaves of finite sets ≃ finite étale X-spaces.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsLocallyConstant.equivPiOneModules` (equivalence): For X connected with geometric point ξ: locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules (Λ finite) ≃ finite Λ-modules with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action; torsion local systems of rank r ↔ modules free of rank r.
- `AdicSpace.LisseSheaf` (structure): Lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves on X_ét (inverse systems, Scholze Definition 8.1) and lisse Ẑ_ℓ-sheaves on X_proét.

**Unit tests.**

- `IsLocallyConstant.test_galois_point` (computation): For X = Spa(K, O_K), F ↦ F_ξ is an equivalence from locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules (Λ finite) to finite Λ-modules with continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-action; torsion local systems of rank r correspond to the modules free of rank r.
- `IsLocallyConstant.test_field_pair_constant` (degenerate): On X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed (C⁺ of any rank) every locally constant sheaf is constant: F ≅ (F_ξ)_X.
- `IsLocallyConstant.test_analytification` (compatibility): For a scheme Y locally of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field and a locally constant sheaf F on Y_ét, the pullback along the analytification morphism of sites (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/analytification-etale-site) is locally constant with the same stalks.
- `IsLocallyConstant.test_extendByZero` (non-example): For the quasi-compact open j: U = {|T| ≤ |p|} of the (connected) closed unit disc, j_!Λ is constructible but not locally constant: its stalks are Λ at geometric points supported in U and 0 at those supported in the nonempty complement, whereas a locally constant sheaf on a connected space has isomorphic stalks.
- `IsLocallyConstant.test_representable` (characterisation): A sheaf of sets with finite stalks is locally constant iff it is representable by a finite étale X-space (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers).

**Acceptance.**

- On X = Spa(K, O_K) (K complete nonarchimedean, rank-one plus ring), locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules (Λ finite) correspond to finite Λ-modules with continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-action, and torsion local systems of rank r to those free of rank r.
- μ_n (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tate-twists) is a torsion local system of rank one over ℤ/n when n is invertible on X.

#### Locally constant sheaves of finite sets are finite étale covers, and π₁-sets on connected spaces

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers` · lemma · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. (a) A sheaf of sets F on X_ét is locally constant with finite values iff F ≅ h_Y := Hom_X(−, Y) for a finite étale X-space Y; Y ↦ h_Y is an equivalence from X_fét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site) to the category of locally constant sheaves of finite sets. (b) If X is connected and ξ a geometric point, F ↦ F_ξ is an equivalence from locally constant sheaves of finite sets to finite sets with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action (π₁ of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category); for a finite ring Λ it restricts to locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules ≃ finite Λ-modules with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action (torsion local systems of rank r ↔ modules free of rank r), compatible with ⊗, Hom and pullback along pointed morphisms. (c) For a finite group G, H^1(X, G_X) is in bijection with isomorphism classes of finite étale G-torsors over X.

**Hypotheses.**

- X locally strongly sheafy analytic; in (b) X connected (|X| connected) with a geometric point ξ.

**Proof.**

1. h_Y is a sheaf and is locally constant: the sheaf property is checked on rational coverings and single faithfully finite étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction), where morphisms into Y = Spa(C) over V = Spa(A) are A-algebra maps C → B (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c)) and the Amitsur complex of a faithfully flat map is exact on algebra maps; local constancy: over a cover on which the degree is constant, Y ×_X Y = Δ(Y) ⊔ Y′ with Δ open and closed (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal) and Y′ → Y finite étale of smaller degree, and induction on the degree splits Y étale-locally (Berkovich 4.4.6).
2. Conversely a locally constant F with finite values is represented on the members of a trivialising covering by finite disjoint unions ⊔_M U_α; the gluing data form a descent datum for finite étale spaces along an étale covering, which is effective: reduce to rational coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent) and single faithfully finite étale maps of affinoids (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction), where descent of the finite projective algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent) keeps étaleness because the trace pairing is perfect after a faithfully flat base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect); the descended space represents F (Berkovich 4.1.8 for the Berkovich analogue).
3. (b) Compose (a) with the fibre functor equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category; for Λ-modules apply it to the finite étale group objects representing torsion local systems.
4. (c) Čech description of H^1 with coefficients in the constant sheaf G_X (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison in degree one for sheaves of groups) and (a) for the torsor, which is finite étale because it is locally a finite disjoint union of copies of the base.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(K, O_K), (b) is the classical equivalence of finite étale K-algebras with finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets.
- On Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, π₁ is trivial and every locally constant sheaf of finite sets is constant.

- [Berkovich-EtaleCohomology-1993], §4.1, Corollary 4.1.9 and remark, p. 85: “We remark that if 9 : Y -> X is an ^tale Galois covering with the Galois group G, then for any abelian sheaf F on X there is a spectral sequence” — Étale Galois coverings as torsors under constant groups, part (c).
- [Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds], §7, proof of Proposition 7.16, p. 36: “If K is not algebraically closed, then for any finite extension L of K with integral closure L+ ⊂ L of K + , the map Spa(L, L+ ) → Spa(K, K + ) is a nonsplit finite étale cover.” — Finite étale covers of Spa(K, K⁺) come from finite extensions of K; they split exactly when K is algebraically closed, which is the π₁ computation in (b).

Then for any $R$-module $M$ the extended cochain complex ( 35.3.4.1 ) is exact.” — Exactness of the Amitsur complex, which gives the sheaf property of h_Y along faithfully finite étale maps.

#### Constructible sheaves in Huber's classical sense

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves` · definition · planet “Constructible sheaf” · packet H0

Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) and Λ a noetherian ring. A subset S ⊆ |X| is constructible if it is a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact open subsets, i.e. Mathlib's Topology.IsConstructible (the Boolean subalgebra generated by the retrocompact opens, which on the quasi-compact quasi-separated |X| are exactly the quasi-compact opens). A sheaf F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is constructible if there is a finite partition |X| = S_1 ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ S_m into locally closed constructible subsets such that for each k the restriction i_{S_k}^{-1}F to the pseudo-adic site (X, S_k)_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site) is locally constant of finite type (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems). For general locally noetherian X, F is constructible if F|_U is constructible for every quasi-compact open U. A complex K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) is constructible if its cohomology sheaves are; D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) denotes the bounded constructible complexes. The condition is on all points of X, including higher-rank points, and on constructible strata that are in general not adic subspaces. This is Huber's notion, the classical analytic constructibility used in H1–H5; it differs from Zariski-constructibility (Bhatt–Hansen), which requires Zariski-locally closed strata of rigid spaces.

**Hypotheses.**

- X qcqs locally noetherian analytic (locally noetherian for the local version); Λ noetherian.
- Strata are locally closed and constructible in |X|; they need not be generalizing or Zariski-closed.

**Construction.**

1. Definition by stratification, using the pseudo-adic restrictions of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site.
2. Well-posedness under refinement: a refinement of a stratification by locally closed constructible subsets keeps local constancy (restriction from (X, S)_ét to (X, T)_ét for T ⊆ S preserves local constancy, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems).
3. Stability properties are ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/constructible-sheaves-stability; the colimit property is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible` (structure): F is constructible: a finite partition into locally closed constructible subsets on whose pseudo-adic sites F is locally constant of finite type.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.ofIsLocallyConstant` (constructor): Locally constant of finite type ⇒ constructible.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.refine` (other): Constructibility is preserved under refinement of the stratification.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.kernel` (other): Kernels, cokernels, images and extensions of constructible sheaves are constructible (abelian subcategory).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.pullback` (functoriality): g^{-1} of a constructible sheaf is constructible for qcqs morphisms of qcqs locally noetherian spaces.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.extendByZero` (functoriality): j_! preserves constructibility for quasi-compact open immersions and u_! for qcqs étale u.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.pushforward_finiteEtale` (functoriality): π_* preserves constructibility for finite étale π.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.stalk_fg` (projection): Every stalk of a constructible sheaf is a finitely generated Λ-module.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.colimit` (characterisation): Every sheaf of Λ-modules on qcqs X is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves (not, in general, of its constructible subsheaves; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible).
- `AdicSpace.DbConstructible` (structure): D^b_c(X_ét, Λ): bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves, a thick triangulated subcategory.
- `AdicSpace.isConstructible_iff_boolean_qcOpens` (compatibility): On qcqs |X|, Topology.IsConstructible S holds iff S lies in the Boolean algebra generated by the quasi-compact opens; preimages along the spectral maps |g| of qcqs morphisms preserve it (Topology.IsConstructible.preimage, retrocompact opens pulling back to retrocompact opens).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.IsConstructible.pseudoAdic` (other): Constructibility on a pseudo-adic space (X, S) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site): a sheaf on (X, S)_ét is constructible if, locally on X, there is a finite partition of S into subsets locally closed and constructible in |X| on each of which (as a pseudo-adic site) the sheaf is locally constant of finite type; for S = |X| this is the definition of the node. Used by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/lambda-pullback-constructible-3-5-6-i for the supports d(X, L). Added by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.

**Unit tests.**

- `IsConstructible.test_localSystem` (computation): A locally constant sheaf of finitely generated Λ-modules is constructible, with the one-stratum partition.
- `IsConstructible.test_zero` (degenerate): The zero sheaf is constructible; on X = ∅ every sheaf is constructible (empty partition).
- `IsConstructible.test_extendByZero_disc` (compatibility): For the qcqs open j of the disc of radius 1/2 in the disc of radius 1, j_!Λ is constructible, and it is not Zariski-constructible in the sense of Bhatt–Hansen.
- `IsConstructible.test_skyscraper` (non-example): The skyscraper sheaf i_{x,*}Λ at a classical point x of the closed unit disc over ℂ_p is not constructible (Bhatt–Hansen, footnote 2): its stalk is Λ at x and 0 at every other point, while every constructible subset containing x contains other points (otherwise the punctured disc U ∖ {x}, for a rational neighbourhood U of x, would be quasi-compact).
- `IsConstructible.test_filtered_colimit` (characterisation): Every sheaf of Λ-modules on a qcqs X is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible).

**Acceptance.**

- Every locally constant sheaf of finite type is constructible (one stratum).
- For the qcqs open immersion j of a closed disc of radius 1/2 into the closed disc of radius 1, j_!Λ is constructible (strata U and its complement) but is not Zariski-constructible (Bhatt–Hansen Warning 3.2 (2)).

#### Stability of constructible sheaves: abelian subcategory, pullback, extension by zero and finite étale pushforward

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/constructible-sheaves-stability` · lemma · packet H0

Let X be a qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic space and Λ noetherian. (a) Constructible sheaves form an abelian subcategory of Sh(X_ét, Λ) stable under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions, and under ⊗_Λ; D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) is a thick triangulated subcategory. (b) For a qcqs morphism g: X′ → X of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, g^{-1} preserves constructibility. (c) For a qcqs étale u: U → X (in particular a quasi-compact open immersion), u_! preserves constructibility; in particular u_!Λ is constructible. (d) For π: X′ → X finite étale, π_* preserves constructibility. (e) Stalks of constructible sheaves are finitely generated.

**Hypotheses.**

- X, X′ qcqs locally noetherian analytic; Λ noetherian; morphisms qcqs.

**Proof.**

1. (a) Given finitely many constructible sheaves, choose a common refinement of their stratifications (finite intersections of locally closed constructible sets are such) and a common trivialising covering of each stratum; on a stratum a map of locally constant sheaves of finite type is étale-locally a map of constant sheaves, so kernels, cokernels and extensions stay locally constant of finite type (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems, abelian closure); restriction i_S^{-1} is exact (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site (i)).
2. (b) Preimages under the spectral map |g| of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact open, so preimages of constructible sets are constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space); g^{-1} commutes with restriction to strata and preserves local constancy.
3. (c) For a quasi-compact open j: U → X, stratify X by a constructible stratification of U together with the closed constructible complement, on which j_!F restricts to 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence (a)). For qcqs étale u: cover U by finitely many qc opens U_k each factoring as an open immersion into a finite étale V_k over a qc open of X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, local description), write u_!G as a quotient of ⊕ (u_k)_!G|_{U_k} with kernel built from the finite intersections, and use (a) with (d) and the open case.
4. (d) X has finitely many connected components (it is qcqs locally noetherian); over each choose a finite étale Galois cover q: X'' → X with group G splitting π (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category). Since q is étale, q^{-1}π_*F(V'') = F(V'' ×_X X′), and X'' ×_X X′ is a disjoint union of copies of X'' given by sections σ_s, so q^{-1}π_*F ≅ ⊕_s σ_s^{-1}F is constructible by (b). Choose a G-stable stratification of X'' on whose strata it is locally constant of finite type (intersect the G-translates of one). For a G-stable constructible C ⊆ X'', q(C) and q(X'' ∖ C) are disjoint because the fibres of q are G-orbits; they are compact for the constructible topology and cover X, so both are constructible. Hence the images of the strata stratify X, and π_*F is locally constant of finite type on each image, because local constancy can be checked after the étale surjection q.
5. (e) The stalk at ξ is a stalk of the restriction to the stratum containing the support of ξ, which is locally a finitely generated constant module.

**Acceptance.**

- For the complement Z of a quasi-compact open U in qcqs X, i_*i^{-1}Λ = coker(j_!Λ → Λ) is constructible by (a) and (c).
- Hansen's use (proof of Proposition 2.4): for a short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 on a dense Zariski-open U ⊆ X in which two of the three terms are locally constant of finite type, all three are constructible on U (Hub96 2.7.3 as cited by Hansen).

#### Every étale sheaf of Λ-modules is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible` · lemma · packet H0

Let X be a qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic space and Λ a noetherian ring. Every F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, though in general not of its constructible subsheaves (on the closed unit disc, coker(j_!Λ → Λ) for the open unit disc j: U → X has stalk Λ at the rank-two point |T| = 1⁻ outside U, while every constructible subsheaf has constructible support in X ∖ U and every constructible set containing that point meets U); in particular every abelian torsion sheaf is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of ℤ/n-modules for varying n. Consequently H^q(X, −) and, for qcqs g: X′ → X, R^q g_* commute with filtered colimits, so statements about torsion sheaves reduce to constructible ones.

**Hypotheses.**

- X qcqs locally noetherian analytic; Λ noetherian.

**Proof.**

1. F is a quotient of ⊕ u_!Λ over pairs (u: U → X qcqs étale, s ∈ F(U)) (each section s gives u_!Λ → F by adjunction, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero); applying the same to the kernel gives a presentation H → G → F → 0 with G, H direct sums of sheaves u_!Λ (ECD proof of Lemma 20.4). Each u_!Λ is compact, Hom(u_!Λ, −) = Γ(U, −) commuting with filtered colimits for qcqs U (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites), so H → G is the filtered colimit of maps H_α → G_α between finite subsums and F = colim_α coker(H_α → G_α), each cokernel constructible by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/constructible-sheaves-stability (a), (c). The images of finite subsums of G in F are quotients of constructible sheaves and need not be constructible.
2. Torsion sheaves: F = colim_n F[n] with F[n] a sheaf of ℤ/n-modules; apply the first part with Λ = ℤ/n.
3. Commutation with filtered colimits: the étale topos of a qcqs space is coherent (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iv)), so DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites applies to H^q(X, −); for R^q g_* use the sheafification description (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification) on qcqs objects.

**Acceptance.**

- Hansen's reduction (proof of Theorem 1.7): H^n(X, −) commutes with filtered colimits, so it suffices to treat constructible sheaves.
- ECD Lemma 20.4: on a spectral space every sheaf of Λ-modules is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves.

#### The Kummer sequence and Hilbert 90 on the étale site

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/kummer-sequence` · lemma · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in O_X(X). Let G_m be the sheaf U ↦ O_U(U)^× on X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf) and μ_n := ker(G_m → G_m, x ↦ x^n). (a) The sequence 1 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 1 is exact on X_ét. (b) Its connecting map gives δ: O(X)^×/(O(X)^×)^n ↪ H^1(X, μ_n) and an exact sequence 0 → O(X)^×/n → H^1(X, μ_n) → H^1(X, G_m)[n] → 0. (c) H^1(X_ét, G_m) ≅ Pic(X) (Hilbert 90), so H^1(X, μ_n) classifies pairs (L, ψ) of a line bundle L and an isomorphism ψ: L^{⊗n} ≅ O_X.

**Hypotheses.**

- n invertible on X (for X over Spa(K, K⁺), n prime to the characteristic of K).
- X locally strongly sheafy analytic; (c) uses étale descent of line bundles.

**Proof.**

1. (a) Left exactness is the definition of μ_n. Surjectivity of x ↦ x^n: for U = Spa(B, B⁺) ∈ X_ét^aff and f ∈ B^×, B′ = B[T]/(T^n − f) is finite free of rank n and étale over B (the discriminant of T^n − f is ± n^n f^{n−1}, a unit), hence Spa of the finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) is a faithfully finite étale covering of U on which f becomes the n-th power of T; general U are covered by basis objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison).
2. (b) Long exact cohomology sequence (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image) with H^0(X, G_m) = O(X)^×.
3. (c) A G_m-torsor on X_ét is an invertible O_{X_ét}-module, and invertible O_{X_ét}-modules are pulled back from line bundles on X_an (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles, vector bundles on X_an and X_ét correspond); torsor classification by H^1 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison in degree one).

**Acceptance.**

- If K contains a primitive n-th root of unity ζ and X lies over Spa(K, K⁺), μ_n ≅ ℤ/n on X_ét via ζ, and H^1(X, ℤ/n) ⊇ O(X)^×/n.
- Non-example: for K imperfect of characteristic p (e.g. K = 𝔽_p((t))) and n = p, T^p − f is not étale, the p-th power map on G_m is not an epimorphism of étale sheaves on Spa(K, O_K) (for f ∈ K^× not a p-th power), and the Artin–Schreier sequence replaces the Kummer sequence.

#### Roots of unity and Tate twists on étale and pro-étale sites

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tate-twists` · construction · packet H0

Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and n ≥ 1 invertible in O_X(X). (i) μ_n := ker(x ↦ x^n on G_m), with μ_n(U) = the group of n-th roots of unity in O_U(U)^× (Mathlib `rootsOfUnity n (O_U(U))`); it is a torsion local system of free ℤ/n-modules of rank one (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems), trivialised on the finite étale cover adjoining a primitive n-th root of unity. (ii) For a ℤ/n-algebra Λ: Λ(1) := Λ ⊗_{ℤ/n} μ_n, Λ(r) := Λ(1)^{⊗_Λ r} for r ≥ 0, Λ(r) := Hom_Λ(Λ(−r), Λ) for r < 0, and F(r) := F ⊗_Λ Λ(r) for F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) and for complexes in D⁺(X_ét, Λ). (iii) For a prime ℓ invertible on X: ℤ_ℓ(1) := (μ_{ℓ^m})_{m ≥ 1} with the ℓ-th power transition maps, a lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaf, and on X_proét (X locally noetherian) Ẑ_ℓ(1) := lim_m ν^*μ_{ℓ^m} with F(r) := F ⊗_{Ẑ_ℓ} Ẑ_ℓ(1)^{⊗r} for sheaves of Ẑ_ℓ-modules. (iv) Canonical isomorphisms Λ(r) ⊗_Λ Λ(s) ≅ Λ(r + s), g^{-1}(F(r)) ≅ (g^{-1}F)(r), (Rg_*K)(r) ≅ Rg_*(K(r)) (projection formula for the locally free rank-one Λ(r)), and stalks (μ_n)_ξ = μ_n(C) at a geometric point Spa(C, C⁺). The exactness of the Kummer sequence is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/kummer-sequence.

**Hypotheses.**

- n (resp. ℓ) invertible on X; Λ a ℤ/n-algebra in (ii).
- Twists are defined for all r ∈ ℤ, with Λ(0) = Λ.

**Construction.**

1. (i) μ_n is a sheaf as a kernel of a map of sheaves (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf). On the cover given over an affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) by B[T]/(Φ_n(T)), finite étale because Φ_n divides the separable polynomial T^n − 1 (n is a unit; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), T is a primitive n-th root of unity (Φ_n(T) and T^d − 1 for d | n, d < n, generate the unit ideal over ℤ[1/n]), so μ_n ≅ ℤ/n there. Stalks: filtered colimits commute with kernels, so (μ_n)_ξ is the n-torsion of O_{X_ét,ξ}^×, which maps bijectively to μ_n(C) because O_{X_ét,ξ} is strictly henselian with residue field separably closed of characteristic prime to n (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)) and T^n − 1 is separable.
2. (ii) Tensor products and internal Hom in Sh(X_ét, Λ) (sheafified), locally free of rank one because μ_n is.
3. (iii) Inverse systems as in Scholze Proposition 6.7; lisse by (i) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems).
4. (iv) Associativity/commutativity of ⊗ and local freeness; g^{-1} is monoidal and g^{-1}μ_n = μ_n (g^{-1}G_m → G_m); projection formula for a locally free rank-one sheaf checked étale-locally where it is Λ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iii)).

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.muN` (constructor): μ_n on X_ét for n invertible on X: the kernel of the n-th power map of G_m.
- `AdicSpace.muN_apply` (simp): μ_n(U) = rootsOfUnity n (O_U(U)).
- `AdicSpace.muN.isLocallyConstant` (other): μ_n is a torsion local system of rank one over ℤ/n.
- `AdicSpace.muN.equivOfPrimitiveRoot` (equivalence): A primitive n-th root of unity in O(X) gives μ_n ≅ ℤ/n on X_ét.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.twist` (constructor): F(r) := F ⊗_Λ Λ(r) for Λ a ℤ/n-algebra and r ∈ ℤ, on sheaves and on D⁺.
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.twistAdd` (relation): F(r)(s) ≅ F(r + s) and Λ(r) ⊗ Λ(s) ≅ Λ(r + s).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.twist_pullback` (compatibility): g^{-1}(F(r)) ≅ (g^{-1}F)(r).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.twist_Rpushforward` (compatibility): (Rg_*K)(r) ≅ Rg_*(K(r)).
- `AdicSpace.EtaleSheaf.stalk_muN` (simp): (μ_n)_ξ ≅ μ_n(C) for ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X.
- `AdicSpace.ZellOne` (constructor): ℤ_ℓ(1) = (μ_{ℓ^m})_m as a lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaf, and Ẑ_ℓ(1) = lim ν^*μ_{ℓ^m} on X_proét.
- `AdicSpace.muN_analytification` (compatibility): Compatibility with the scheme μ_n under the analytification morphism of sites.

**Unit tests.**

- `muN_test_stalk` (computation): At a geometric point ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X, (μ_n)_ξ ≅ μ_n(C) ≅ ℤ/n (after choosing a primitive root in C).
- `twist_test_zero` (degenerate): Λ(0) = Λ, F(0) = F, and μ_1 is the trivial sheaf.
- `muN_test_rootsOfUnity` (compatibility): For U ∈ X_ét, μ_n(U) = rootsOfUnity n (O_U(U)) (Mathlib); and λ_X^{-1}μ_{n,Y} ≅ μ_{n,Y^ad} for the analytification of a scheme Y locally of finite type over K.
- `twist_test_add` (characterisation): Λ(r) ⊗_Λ Λ(s) ≅ Λ(r + s) canonically, and F(r)(s) ≅ F(r + s).
- `kummer_test_char_p` (non-example): For K = 𝔽_p((t)) (or any imperfect K of characteristic p) and X = Spa(K, O_K), the p-th power map on G_m is not surjective as a map of étale sheaves (t is not a p-th power in any finite separable extension of K), so there is no Kummer sequence for n = p; twists are defined only for n invertible on X.

**Acceptance.**

- For X over Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}), a compatible system of roots of unity gives ℤ_ℓ(1) ≅ ℤ_ℓ on X_ét.
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and a prime ℓ ≠ p with ℓ ∤ p − 1, μ_ℓ is a nonconstant local system (μ_ℓ(ℚ_p) = 1), whose Galois module is the cyclotomic character mod ℓ.

### Huber tilde-limits and cohomological continuity

Huber's tilde-limit X ∼ lim X_i requires a homeomorphism onto the inverse limit of the underlying spaces and, separately, the affinoid density condition. The adic spectrum of a colimit of Huber pairs is the limit of the spectra; the affinoid criterion recognises completed colimits and colimit-presented affinoids as tilde-limits, with the topology hypothesis (T), or in the Tate form the congruence condition (P2), made explicit, since density and a plus-ring condition alone do not suffice; density passes to rational subsets defined at a finite level; strict localisations are tilde-limits of their affinoid étale neighbourhoods; colimit-presented tilde-limits are stable under base change; the étale site of a tilde-limit is the colimit of the étale sites (Huber 2.4.4, proved for locally colimit-presented tilde-limits, the general case being a gap); and étale cohomology is continuous along tilde-limits (Huber 2.4.6).

#### Huber tilde-limits X ∼ lim X_i: the topological condition and the density condition

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit` · definition · planet “Huber tilde-limit” · packet H0

Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ X_i a functor from I to analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5; every point analytic) whose transition morphisms f_a: X_j → X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the X_i themselves need not be quasi-compact), X an analytic adic space and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i)_i a compatible family (f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i). The pair (X, φ) is a tilde-limit, written X ∼ lim_i X_i, if the two following conditions hold, which are recorded as separate predicates. (a) Topological condition `IsTildeLimit.Homeomorph`: the continuous map |X| → lim_i |X_i| into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`) is a homeomorphism. (b) Density condition `IsTildeLimit.Dense`: every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X such that the subring E_U := ⋃ im(O_{X_i}(V) → A), the union over i ∈ I and over open V ⊆ X_i with φ_i(U) ⊆ V, is dense in A (Huber's form; Scholze–Weinstein take the colimit only over the open affinoids V = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ⊆ X_i through which U → X_i factors, and that colimit maps into E_U, so their condition implies (b) for the same U). Variant for pseudo-adic spaces (Huber's Definition 2.4.2): for quasi-compact quasi-separated pseudo-adic spaces (X_i, S_i) and (X, S) with adic transition morphisms (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site), (a) asks S → lim_i S_i to be a homeomorphism for the subspace topologies and (b) is asked at every x ∈ S, U an affinoid open neighbourhood of x in X. Conventions pinned: (i) a tilde-limit is not a categorical limit in adic spaces — X ∼ X₀ may hold with X ≇ X₀, and inverse limits of adic spaces rarely exist; the notation ∼ is never read as lim; (ii) (a) and (b) are independent and both required; (iii) the residue-field variant ∼′ of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 (density of colim k(x_i) in k(x)) is weaker and is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit; (iv) for perfectoid X this predicate is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, which imports it.

**Hypotheses.**

- I small cofiltered; transition maps of (X_i) quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1 generality).
- X and all X_i analytic adic spaces (sheafy, anchor Layer 5); X need not be quasi-compact or locally noetherian.
- Huber's own setting (2.4.1–2.4.2: the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated pseudo-adic spaces, not necessarily analytic, with adic morphisms) overlaps this node in the qcqs analytic case, where every morphism is adic.

**Construction.**

1. Definition as the conjunction of the two predicates; (a) uses mathlib:TopCat.limitCone, (b) the structure sheaves of X and of the X_i on open subsets.
2. Pseudo-adic variant: the same with the subspaces S, S_i and ambient affinoid neighbourhoods, as in Huber 2.4.2; for S = |X|, S_i = |X_i| it is the adic version.
3. Spectrality (API): if all X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, lim |X_i| is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces), hence so is |X| under (a).
4. Reindexing (API): along an initial functor J → I both the limit of topological spaces and the density union are unchanged.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` (structure): The predicate X ∼ lim X_i on a compatible family φ from X to a cofiltered system with qcqs transition maps.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.Homeomorph` (structure): Condition (a): |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.Dense` (structure): Condition (b): local density of ⋃ im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U)) for an affinoid neighbourhood U of each point.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (projection): The homeomorphism |X| ≃ lim |X_i|.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.dense` (projection): For x ∈ X, an affinoid U ∋ x with E_U dense in O_X(U).
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.mk` (constructor): From proofs of (a) and (b).
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofIso` (functoriality): Transport along an isomorphism X ≅ X′ commuting with the cones.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.reindex` (functoriality): Invariance under an initial change of index category.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.const` (example): An isomorphism X ≅ X₀ is a tilde-limit of the constant one-object system.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (other): If all X_i are qcqs, |X| is spectral and the φ_i are spectral maps.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.restrictRational` (functoriality): Restriction to preimages of rational subsets defined at a finite level (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction).
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofCompletedColimit` (constructor): The affinoid criterion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion).
- `PseudoAdicSpace.IsTildeLimit` (compatibility): Huber's pseudo-adic version for qcqs pseudo-adic spaces; agrees with AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit for (X, |X|).
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.of_bijective` (characterisation): Huber's criterion (Remark 2.4.3 (i), as used by AdicSpacesPartII:R5/tilde-limit-base-change): if all X_i are qcqs, |X| → lim |X_i| is bijective, and every x ∈ X has an affinoid neighbourhood U satisfying (b) together with i ∈ I and an open W ⊆ X_i with x ∈ φ_i^{-1}(W) ⊆ U, then X ∼ lim X_i. Proof: a rational subset of U is unchanged when its defining functions are replaced by close elements of E_U (Huber 1993, Lemma 3.11), so it is the preimage of an open of some X_j lying over W; hence the bijection is open.
- `AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.dense_of_affinoidDense` (relation): If the colimit of O(V) over open affinoids V ⊆ X_i through which U → X_i factors has dense image in O_X(U) (Scholze–Weinstein's form), then (b) holds for U; for perfectoid X the converse is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis.

**Unit tests.**

- `IsTildeLimit.test_completed_colimit` (computation): For K complete nonarchimedean of residue characteristic p, Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ∼ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩), the left side being the completed colimit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion).
- `IsTildeLimit.test_const` (degenerate): For the one-object category and an isomorphism φ: X ≅ X₀, X ∼ X₀.
- `IsTildeLimit.test_not_categorical` (non-example): For a complete nonarchimedean field K, Spa(K, K°) ∼ Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε) along K[ε] → K (both spaces are one point and K[ε] → K is surjective), although the two adic spaces are not isomorphic.
- `IsTildeLimit.test_density_needed` (non-example): Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) (one object) satisfies (a) (both are one point) but not (b) (ℚ_p is not dense in ℂ_p).
- `IsTildeLimit.test_topology_needed` (non-example): The closed unit disc D mapped into the first summand of the constant system D ⊔ D satisfies (b) (O(D) × O(D) → O(D) is surjective) but not (a).
- `IsTildeLimit.test_huber_compat` (compatibility): For X and all X_i quasi-compact quasi-separated, X ∼ lim X_i iff (X, |X|) ∼ lim (X_i, |X_i|) in the pseudo-adic sense of Huber's Definition 2.4.2.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 / ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion: the completed colimit of a system of affinoid rings with compatible rings and ideals of definition is a tilde-limit.
- Strict localisations: Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim V over affinoid étale neighbourhoods of a geometric point ξ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit).

**Used by.**

- Huber 1996, §§2.4–2.6 (decomposition): X ∼ lim X_i for qcqs pseudo-adic spaces; 2.4.4 (étale topos), 2.4.6 (continuity), 2.5.12 (strict localisation), 2.6.1 (stalks)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit (P0 request): the perfectoid tilde-limit is this predicate for perfectoid X, in Scholze–Weinstein 2.4.1 generality
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers (P8 request): the inverse-limit topology and affinoid density, and density of lim O(V_i) in O(V)
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-tilde-limit (R5 request): X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim X_n ×_L U via the affinoid criterion
- ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation: X ×_Y Y(ξ) ∼ lim X ×_Y V over étale neighbourhoods
- ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison (3.5.8–3.5.10): limit steps over strict localisations Y_∞ = lim Y_i and their formal completions
- Scholze–Weinstein §§2.4, 6.3; Scholze torsion paper III.1.2: infinite-level Lubin–Tate and Shimura spaces as tilde-limits

#### The adic spectrum of a colimit of Huber pairs is the limit of the adic spectra

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair` · lemma · packet H0

Let I be a small filtered category and (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} a diagram of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with continuous transition maps, together with rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i mapped into one another and finitely generated ideals of definition I_i ⊆ A_{i,0} with I_j = I_i A_{j,0} for i → j (the transition maps are adic). Let A := colim_i A_i with the topology in which A_0 := colim_i A_{i,0} is an open subring carrying the I-adic topology, I := colim_i I_i, and A⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺. Then: (i) (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (A, A⁺) are adic morphisms of Huber pairs; (ii) the map Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) induced by the Tau Ceti maps `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap` is a homeomorphism onto the limit of topological spaces; (iii) every rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺); (iv) for the completion (Â, Â⁺), Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets, so (ii)–(iii) hold for Spa(Â, Â⁺); (v) colim_i A_i → Â has dense image. (vi) Tate re-topologisation: if (A, A⁺) is a Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A⁺, the Huber ring A′ equal to A as a ring, with A⁺ an open ring of definition carrying the ϖ-adic topology, has Spa(A′, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) with the same rational subsets (both are the valuations v with v(A⁺) ≤ 1 and v(ϖ) cofinal); (vii) consequently, for a filtered system of complete Tate Huber pairs with a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (no compatible rings of definition needed), lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spa(L̂⁺[1/ϖ], L̂⁺), where L̂⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of L⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺. In the Tate case with compatible rings of definition this is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs.

**Hypotheses.**

- I filtered; in (i)–(v) compatible rings of definition and finitely generated ideals of definition with I_j = I_i A_{j,0}; in (vi)–(vii) complete Tate pairs with a compatible pseudouniformiser.
- No perfectoid or noetherian hypothesis.

**Proof.**

1. (i) A_0 is an open subring with a finitely generated ideal I (generated by the image of generators of any I_i); A⁺ is integrally closed in A (an integral equation and its coefficients live at a finite stage, where A_i⁺ is integrally closed), open (it contains the image of an open subgroup I_i^N A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i⁺) and consists of power-bounded elements (images of power-bounded elements under continuous maps).
2. (ii) Points: valuations on A are compatible systems of valuations on the A_i, since every finite set of elements and relations of A comes from a finite stage (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap). Continuity: by Wedhorn Theorem 7.10 and Remark 7.11 (1) (Tau Ceti `mem_spvOfIdeal_extendedIdealOfDefinition_of_isContinuous` and `PairOfDefinition.isContinuous_of_forall_cofinalValue`) a valuation is continuous iff v(a) is cofinal for the finitely many generators a of the ideal of definition, which are images of generators of I_i; the plus-ring condition is checked on each A_i⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff). Hence the map is a continuous bijection (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap).
3. (iii) For R(T/s) with T·A open, finitely many elements of T, s, and of I^N ⊆ T·A are defined at a stage i with I_i^N ⊆ T_i·A_i, so R(T/s) is the preimage of R(T_i/s_i) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset); rational subsets form a basis, so the bijection is open, hence a homeomorphism.
4. (iv) Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 (Huber 1993 Proposition 3.9): Spa of the completion of an affinoid ring maps homeomorphically onto Spa of the ring, matching rational subsets; the anchor lists it but it is not a pinned declaration (request to tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets).
5. (v) mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe.
6. (vi) For a Tate ring, continuity of a valuation is cofinality of v(ϖ) for any ring of definition containing ϖ (Wedhorn Remark 7.11 (1) with I = ϖA_0), and T·A is open iff T generates the unit ideal (an open ideal contains a unit ϖ^N); both descriptions are independent of the choice of ring of definition, and A⁺ is open and bounded for its own ϖ-adic topology.
7. (vii) Apply (vi) to each A_i (ring of definition A_i⁺, ideal ϖA_i⁺; the transition maps stay continuous because ϖ^n A_j⁺ ⊇ image of ϖ^n A_i⁺), then (i)–(iv) to the resulting system, whose colimit has ring of definition L⁺ and completion L̂⁺[1/ϖ].

**Acceptance.**

- For a constant system the statement is Spa(A, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺).
- For A_n = K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ over a complete nonarchimedean field K: Spa of the completed colimit K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩).
