#### The affinoid criterion: completed colimits and colimit-presented affinoids are tilde-limits

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion` · theorem · packet H0

(1) Huber-pair form. Let (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} be a filtered system of complete Huber pairs with rings of definition and finitely generated ideals of definition as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair, such that each X_i := Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is an adic space (A_i sheafy), and let (B, B⁺) be a complete Huber pair with compatible adic morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (B, B⁺) such that X := Spa(B, B⁺) is an adic space. Suppose (T) the closure B_0 of the image of colim A_{i,0} is a ring of definition of B with ideal of definition generated by the image of I_i (the topology of B is the colimit topology), (D) colim A_i → B has dense image, and (P) B⁺ is the closure of the image of colim A_i⁺; equivalently, (B, B⁺) is the completed colimit (Â, Â⁺). Then X ∼ lim_i X_i (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) with the density condition holding globally for U = X. (2) Tate form (colimit-presented affinoids). Let the A_i be complete Tate rings with a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ, L⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺, and (C, C⁺) a complete Tate Huber pair with compatible morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (C, C⁺) such that (P2) the induced maps L⁺/ϖ^n L⁺ → C⁺/ϖ^n C⁺ are isomorphisms for all n ≥ 1; call Spa(C, C⁺) colimit-presented by (Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)). Then Spa(C, C⁺) ∼ lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) with global density, the kernel of colim A_i → C lies in ⋂_n ϖ^n L⁺, and every rational subset of Spa(C, C⁺) is the preimage of one at a finite stage. The completed colimit in the Tate case is colimit-presented. (3) Condition (T), resp. (P2), cannot be replaced by density and a plus-ring condition alone (non-example below).

**Hypotheses.**

- Complete Huber (resp. Tate) pairs; all Spa's involved are adic spaces (sheafy). This restricts to honest adic spaces: Scholze–Weinstein state Proposition 2.4.2 for the uncompleted colimit in their larger category of adic spaces (Definition 2.1.5), where Spa(A, A⁺) = Spa(Â, Â⁺) is defined without completeness or sheafiness, so the source statement is correct as written there.
- The topology on the target must be the colimit topology (T), or the plus rings must agree modulo every power of ϖ (P2).

**Proof.**

1. (1)(a) By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair (ii) and (iv), Spa(B, B⁺) = Spa(Â, Â⁺) → lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a homeomorphism. (1)(b) For U = X and V = X_i, E_X contains the image of colim A_i, dense in B by (D) (spa-of-colimit (v)). The equivalence of (T)+(D)+(P) with (B, B⁺) ≅ (Â, Â⁺) is the uniqueness of completions.
2. (2)(a) By spa-of-colimit (vi)–(vii), lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spa(L̂⁺[1/ϖ], L̂⁺) and Spa(C, C⁺) ≅ Spa(Ĉ⁺[1/ϖ], Ĉ⁺) (ϖ-adic completions); by (P2), L̂⁺ ≅ Ĉ⁺, compatibly with the maps, so Spa(C, C⁺) → lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a homeomorphism and rational subsets come from a finite stage (spa-of-colimit (iii)).
3. (2)(b) Density: C⁺ = im(L⁺) + ϖ^n C⁺ for every n by (P2), and ϖ^n C⁺ is open, so the image of colim A_i is dense in C. Kernel: if f ∈ colim A_i maps to 0, then ϖ^k f ∈ L⁺ for some k and ϖ^k f maps into ϖ^m C⁺ for every m, so ϖ^k f ∈ ϖ^m L⁺ for every m by (P2).
4. (2) for completed colimits: Â⁺/ϖ^n = A⁺/ϖ^n because ϖ^n A⁺ is open in A⁺.
5. Non-example: the constant system A_0 = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ with (B, B⁺) = (ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩, the integral closure of im(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) + B°°): the image is dense (polynomials are dense) and B⁺ is the ring of integral elements generated by the image, but Spa(B, B⁺) maps onto the closure of {|T| ≤ |p|} in Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩), not onto the whole disc, so (a) fails; here (T) and (P2) both fail (T/p ∈ B° is not approximated modulo p by elements of ℤ_p⟨T⟩).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2: Spa(A, A⁺) ∼ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) for the colimit with its colimit topology.
- Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ∼ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) for any complete nonarchimedean K of residue characteristic p (the perfectoid case is PerfectoidSpaces P7).
- Serves the AdicSpacesPartII R5 request (affinoid criterion for X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim X_n ×_L U), with hypothesis (T) or (P2) made explicit: density of colim A_n in A and the plus-ring condition do not suffice.

(P2), is part of the criterion.

#### Density on rational subsets defined at a finite level, and restriction of tilde-limits

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction` · lemma · packet H0

Let X ∼ lim_i X_i be a tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) and U ⊆ X an affinoid open satisfying the density condition, i.e. E_U = ⋃ im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U)) is dense in O_X(U). (a) If i ∈ I, V ⊆ X_i is an open affinoid with φ_i(U) ⊆ V and R = R_V(T/s) a rational subset of V, then U′ := U ∩ φ_i^{-1}(R) (a rational subset of U) satisfies the density condition. (b) If all X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) and X = Spa(A, A⁺) are affinoid and colim_i A_i → A has dense image, then for every rational subset W_i ⊆ X_i with preimages W_j ⊆ X_j (i → j) and W ⊆ X, colim_j O(W_j) → O(W) has dense image, and W ∼ lim_j W_j. (c) More generally, for an open U_i ⊆ X_i with preimages U_j, U, the restriction U ∼ lim_j U_j holds whenever U is covered by affinoids satisfying the density condition (for example by (a)). The density of colim O(W_j) in O(W) for an arbitrary affinoid W ∼ lim W_j is not asserted; it is supplied under the hypotheses above.

**Hypotheses.**

- Tilde-limit X ∼ lim X_i; in (b) global density on the affinoid X.
- Rational subsets defined at a finite level.

**Proof.**

1. (a) Pull T, s back to O(U); U′ = R_U(φ_i^*T/φ_i^*s) and O(U′) is the completion of O(U)[1/s] for the rational topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization), in which the image of O(U)[1/s] is dense (mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe). For (j, V′) with φ_j(U) ⊆ V′ ⊆ f_a^{-1}(V), the open V′ ∩ f_a^{-1}(R) contains φ_j(U′) and s is invertible on it, so E_{U′} ⊇ {e/s^m : e ∈ E_U}. Multiplication by s^{-m} is continuous on O(U′) and O(U) → O(U′) is continuous, so E_U dense in O(U) gives {e/s^m} dense in the image of O(U)[1/s], hence in O(U′).
2. (b) Apply (a) with U = X, V = X_i; the topological condition for W: |W| = φ_i^{-1}|W_i| and preimages commute with limits of topological spaces, so |W| ≅ lim_j |W_j| (restriction of the homeomorphism).
3. (c) The topological condition restricts as in (b); density is local by definition.

**Acceptance.**

- For the affinoid criterion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion) every rational subset defined at a finite level satisfies global density.
- Serves the PerfectoidSpaces P8 request (density of lim O(V_i) in O(V)) whenever V is a rational subset defined at a finite level of a globally dense affinoid.

#### The strict localisation of an analytic adic space is a tilde-limit of its affinoid étale neighbourhoods

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit` · lemma · packet H0

Let Y be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → Y a geometric point with support y, N(ξ)^aff the cofiltered category of étale neighbourhoods (V, v̄) of ξ with V affinoid Tate (cofinal in N(ξ), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation), L := colim_{N(ξ)^aff} O(V) = O_{Y_ét,ξ}, L⁺ := colim O⁺(V), m_ξ the maximal ideal of the local ring L, κ(ξ) = L/m_ξ, and (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) the completion of (κ(ξ), κ(ξ)⁺) where κ(ξ)⁺ is the valuation ring of the valuation at the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)). Then: (a) L⁺ is the preimage of κ(ξ)⁺ in L, and m_ξ ⊆ ϖ^n L⁺ for every n and every pseudouniformiser ϖ of a neighbourhood; (b) the maps L⁺/ϖ^n → C_ξ⁺/ϖ^n are isomorphisms for all n, i.e. Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is colimit-presented by the neighbourhoods in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2); (c) hence Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} V is a Huber tilde-limit with global density, and |Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺)| ≅ lim_{N(ξ)} |V|, which is clause (b) of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic, obtained here without its shrinking step; (d) (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is an algebraically closed affinoid field with C_ξ⁺ = C⁺ ∩ C_ξ, and the valuation rings of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) correspond to the vertical generisations of y.

**Hypotheses.**

- Y locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ a geometric point with C⁺ of any rank (higher-rank field pairs are kept).

**Proof.**

1. (a) L = colim O_{V,v} over the images v of the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (ii)–(iii)); in each stalk O⁺_{V,v} is the preimage of the valuation ring of k(v) and the maximal ideal is the support of the valuation (Wedhorn Proposition 8.6); passing to the colimit gives L⁺ = preimage of κ(ξ)⁺. For f with v(f) = 0, the rational subset {|f| ≤ |ϖ^n|} is an open neighbourhood of v, hence of the image of the lift (open sets are stable under generisation), and on it f/ϖ^n ∈ O⁺ (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52 (1)), so f ∈ ϖ^n L⁺.
2. (b) Surjectivity: κ(ξ)⁺ = L⁺/m_ξ is dense in C_ξ⁺ and ϖ^n C_ξ⁺ is open. Injectivity: if ℓ ∈ L⁺ maps into ϖ^n C_ξ⁺, then ℓ/ϖ^n has valuation ≤ 1 at the closed point, so ℓ/ϖ^n ∈ L⁺ by (a).
3. (c) ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2), the maps Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) → V being induced by the lifts of ξ.
4. (d) C_ξ algebraically closed and C_ξ⁺ = C⁺ ∩ C_ξ: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a); the valuation of κ(ξ) restricts to that of k(y) along the separable algebraic extension κ(ξ)/k(y), which induces a bijection on convex subgroups, and the canonical map Spa κ(y) → Y is a homeomorphism onto the vertical generisations of y (Wedhorn §8.1).

**Acceptance.**

- For Y = Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank 2 and ξ supported at the closed point, Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) has two points and is the tilde-limit of the Spa(L, L⁺) over finite separable L/K inside C (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (c)).
- For Y a rigid space and ξ of rank one, this is the étale fibre Sp(F_e) of de Jong–van der Put §3.3.

#### Base change of colimit-presented tilde-limits

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change` · lemma · packet H0

Let Z = Spa(C, C⁺) be colimit-presented by a system Z_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) of complete Tate affinoids with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2); examples: completed colimits, and strict localisations by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit). (a) If (A_{i₀}, A_{i₀}⁺) → (B, B⁺) is an adic morphism of complete Huber pairs, topologically of finite type or étale, such that the completed tensor products B_i := B ⊗̂_{A_{i₀}} A_i (i over i₀) and B_C := B ⊗̂_{A_{i₀}} C are sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), then Spa(B_C) is colimit-presented by (Spa(B_i)), hence Spa(B_C) ∼ lim_i Spa(B_i). (b) Globally: if Y(ξ) ∼ lim V is the strict localisation of a locally strongly sheafy analytic Y and f: X → Y is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type, then X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} X ×_Y V, locally on X colimit-presented; likewise for the base change of any colimit-presented system along such a morphism. The statement for arbitrary tilde-limits and arbitrary maps Y_i → X_i (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3, proved there by reference to Huber's Remark 2.4.3) is not claimed.

**Hypotheses.**

- Colimit-presented tilde-limits of complete Tate affinoids; B topologically of finite type or étale over A_{i₀}, with sheafy completed tensor products.
- For (b), f quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type, so that the fibre products exist (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence).

**Proof.**

1. (a) Points, without assuming (P2) for B: put M_i := B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} A_i⁺, M := colim_i M_i = B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} L⁺ and M_C := B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} C⁺, so that M_i[1/ϖ] = B ⊗_{A_{i₀}} A_i and M_C[1/ϖ] = B ⊗_{A_{i₀}} C. By the construction of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product: ring of definition from B_0 ⊗ A_{i,0}, plus ring the completed integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ A_i⁺), Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 and tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure, a point of Spa(B_i) is a valuation v of M_i[1/ϖ] with v(M_i) ≤ 1 and v(ϖ) cofinal, and likewise for Spa(B_C) with M_C; so lim_i Spa(B_i) is the set of such valuations on M[1/ϖ] (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair (vi)–(vii)). Such a valuation is continuous for the ϖ-adic topology and so corresponds to a unique one on the ϖ-adic completion M̂, and likewise for M_C. By right exactness of ⊗ and (P2) for the A_i, M/ϖ^n = B⁺/ϖ^n ⊗ L⁺/ϖ^n ≅ B⁺/ϖ^n ⊗ C⁺/ϖ^n = M_C/ϖ^n for all n, compatibly, so M̂ ≅ M̂_C and Spa(B_C) → lim_i Spa(B_i) is bijective. Rational subsets are defined at a finite stage (spa-of-colimit (iii)), so it is a homeomorphism. Density: B ⊗ L is dense in B ⊗ C for the topology with ring of definition the image of B_0 ⊗ C_0, because L is dense in C, so colim B_i → B_C has dense image.
2. Plus rings modulo ϖ^n: an element ℓ ∈ L_B whose image in B_C has |ℓ| ≤ |ϖ^n| at every point of Spa(B_C) (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52 (1): i.e. lies in ϖ^n B_C⁺) satisfies |ℓ| ≤ |ϖ^n| on some stage Spa(B_i): the set {|ℓ| > |ϖ^n|} ⊆ Spa(B_i) is closed constructible with empty preimage in the limit, so it is empty at a finite stage (Stacks Tag 0A30); hence ℓ ∈ ϖ^n L_B⁺. With density of the image of L_B⁺ modulo the open subgroup ϖ^n B_C⁺ this gives L_B⁺/ϖ^n ≅ B_C⁺/ϖ^n, i.e. (P2).
3. (b) Cover X by finitely many affinoids X_k mapping into affinoids of Y pulled back from a finite stage; fibre products of affinoids are Spa of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product; for étale V over an affinoid, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change); apply (a) to each X_k and to their pairwise intersections, and glue: the topological condition is local over a cover by preimages of opens at a finite stage, and density is local by definition.

**Acceptance.**

- For f: X → Y and ξ a rank-one geometric point of a rigid space Y, X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is the étale fibre X_e of de Jong–van der Put, and (b) is the tilde-limit form of their Lemma 3.7.1.
- For an étale V_{i₀} → Z_{i₀} the base change is the étale case of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3 for colimit-presented systems.

#### The étale site of a tilde-limit is the colimit of the étale sites (Huber 2.4.4)

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit` · lemma · packet H0

Let X ∼ lim_i X_i be a tilde-limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (locally noetherian in Huber's setting), the index category having a final object 0. Then: (i) every quasi-compact quasi-separated étale Y → X is isomorphic to Y_i ×_{X_i} X for some i and some quasi-compact quasi-separated étale Y_i → X_i; (ii) for Y_i, Y′_i étale qcqs over X_i, Hom_X(Y_i ×_{X_i} X, Y′_i ×_{X_i} X) = colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j, Y′_i ×_{X_i} X_j); (iii) a finite family of such maps is a covering over X iff it is one over some X_j; hence (iv) the site of qcqs étale X-spaces is the filtered 2-colimit of the sites of qcqs étale X_i-spaces, and the étale topos of X is the projective limit of the fibred topos (X_{i,ét}~)_i. This is proved here for tilde-limits that are locally colimit-presented (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change: completed colimits of affinoid systems, strict localisations and their base changes along qcqs morphisms locally of weakly finite type), which covers every use in H0; for arbitrary tilde-limits of qcqs locally noetherian spaces (Huber Proposition 2.4.4) the finite étale descent step rests on Huber's book and is recorded as a gap.

**Hypotheses.**

- X, X_i qcqs, locally strongly sheafy analytic; I with final object 0.
- Complete proof for locally colimit-presented tilde-limits; the general Huber case is a recorded gap.

**Proof.**

1. Opens: quasi-compact opens of |X| ≅ lim |X_i| come from quasi-compact opens at a finite stage, and inclusions and equalities of such opens are detected at a finite stage (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces; Stacks Tag 0A30), the X_i being spectral.
2. Reduction: étale maps are locally an open immersion into a finite étale space over an open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), so it suffices to descend finite étale algebras, their morphisms and surjectivity over the affinoids of a finite cover by rational subsets defined at a finite stage, which are again colimit-presented: a rational localisation is a base change along a topologically finite type map (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change (a); density by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction).
3. Finite étale descent for Z = Spa(C, C⁺) colimit-presented by Spa(A_i, A_i⁺): FÉt(L) = 2-colim FÉt(A_i) for L = colim A_i, finite étale algebras being of finite presentation (Stacks Tag 00QO for morphisms, and descent of finitely presented algebras for objects). The plus ring A_i⁺ of a complete Tate ring is henselian along ϖ: it is the filtered union of the ϖ-adically complete rings A_i⁺ ∩ R over rings of definition R (Stacks Tags 0ALJ, 0FWT); hence L⁺ = colim A_i⁺ is henselian along ϖ (0FWT), and likewise C⁺. By PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (a) (R = L⁺, resp. C⁺, t = ϖ): FÉt(L) ≃ FÉt(L̂⁺[1/ϖ]) and FÉt(C) ≃ FÉt(Ĉ⁺[1/ϖ]); the ϖ-adic completions agree by (P2), so FÉt(C) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(A_i). Surjectivity of finite étale maps is detected on points, hence at a finite stage.
4. Gap (general case): for an arbitrary Huber tilde-limit the affinoids of X are not known to be colimit-presented, and Huber's proof of 2.4.4 is not public.
5. (iv) from (i)–(iii): the description of projective limits of fibred topoi by the 2-colimit of the underlying sites (SGA 4 VI 8.2), requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0.

**Acceptance.**

- For the strict localisation Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim V, every qcqs étale space over Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is a finite disjoint union of open subspaces of copies of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split) and descends to a neighbourhood.
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 7.17 is the perfectoid analogue (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison), proved "as Huber 2.4.4" with the same open-immersion/finite-étale factorisation.

#### Continuity of étale cohomology along tilde-limits (Huber 2.4.6)

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity` · theorem · planet “Cohomological continuity” · packet H0

Let I be a small cofiltered category with final object 0, (X_i) a system of quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces with quasi-compact quasi-separated transition maps, X a quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space with X ∼ lim_i X_i (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) for which the conclusion of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit holds (in particular every colimit-presented tilde-limit). Let F_0 be a sheaf of sets (resp. groups, resp. abelian groups or Λ-modules) on X_{0,ét}, with pullbacks F_i on X_{i,ét} and F on X_ét. Then for n = 0 (resp. n ∈ {0, 1}, resp. all n ≥ 0) the natural map colim_i H^n(X_i, F_i) → H^n(X, F) is bijective. For a bounded-below complex K_0 the same holds for hypercohomology. The same statement holds for pseudo-adic tilde-limits of qcqs pseudo-adic spaces whose étale topoi satisfy the descent of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit; that general hypothesis is exactly where Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 enters.

**Hypotheses.**

- X, X_i qcqs; transition maps qcqs; final object 0; F_0 pulled back from X_0.
- The étale topos of X is the projective limit of the (X_{i,ét}~) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit), proved for colimit-presented tilde-limits.

**Proof.**

1. By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit the site of qcqs étale X-spaces is the filtered 2-colimit of the sites of qcqs étale X_i-spaces along continuous finite-limit-preserving base-change functors, every covering of X coming from a finite stage.
2. All these sites are coherent (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iv)), and cohomology on a projective limit of coherent topoi of a sheaf pulled back from a stage is the colimit of the cohomologies (SGA 4 VI 8.7.7; requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0, stage-level prerequisite), in degrees 0, ≤ 1, all n for sets, groups, abelian groups; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites gives the underlying commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits on each coherent stage.
3. Hypercohomology of bounded-below complexes: induction on the length of truncations and the five lemma, then passage to the limit along the canonical filtration (the maps are compatible with the connecting maps).

**Acceptance.**

- Continuity along strict localisations: colim_{N(ξ)} H^n(X ×_Y V, F) = H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), F) (the input of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation).
- For X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ∼ lim Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) and a torsion sheaf F_0: H^n(X, F) = colim H^n(Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩), F_n).
- Česnavičius (4.10.7): on a common-ideal perfectoid completed-colimit system whose qcqs étale site is a filtered 2-colimit, finite locally constant abelian coefficient cohomology is the filtered colimit in every fixed degree.

### The stalk formula over strict localisations

Stalks of higher direct images are colimits over étale neighbourhoods, and for a qcqs morphism locally of weakly finite type they are the cohomology of the fibre over the strict localisation (Huber 2.6.1), at geometric points with plus rings of any rank.

#### Stalks of higher direct images as colimits over étale neighbourhoods

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-of-higher-direct-image-as-colimit` · lemma · packet H0

Let g: X′ → X be a morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, F ∈ Sh(X′_ét, Λ) and ξ a geometric point of X with category of étale neighbourhoods N(ξ) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation). Then for every q ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism (R^q g_*F)_ξ ≅ colim_{(V, v̄) ∈ N(ξ)} H^q(V ×_X X′, F), and the colimit may be taken over the cofinal subcategory N(ξ)^aff of affinoid neighbourhoods; it is compatible with the connecting maps in F. The same holds for ν: (R^qν_*F)_ξ ≅ colim_{N(ξ)} H^q(V, F) with V regarded in X_proét (X locally noetherian).

**Hypotheses.**

- g arbitrary; ξ a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank).

**Proof.**

1. R^q g_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(U ×_X X′, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification).
2. The stalk of a presheaf at a point of a site equals the stalk of its sheafification (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso: presheafToSheaf ⋙ sheafFiber ≅ presheafFiber), and the presheaf stalk is the colimit over the category of elements, which is N(ξ) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafFiber).
3. Cofinality of affinoid neighbourhoods: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (ii) with AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (a).

**Acceptance.**

- For g finite étale, V ×_X X′ splits over small neighbourhoods into copies of V (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers), and the formula gives (g_*F)_ξ = ⊕ over the geometric points of X′ above ξ of F at those points, and R^q g_*F = 0 for q > 0 after ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation.

Take an etale point e of X and denote by Ye the (etale) bre of f at e.” — The rigid-analytic statement comparing (R^q f_*S)_e with the étale fibre starts from this colimit description.
- [Scholze-PadicHodgeRigid-2013], §3, proof of Corollary 3.17, p. 20: “We recall that for any i ≥ 0, Ri ν∗ ν ∗ F is the sheaf on Xét associated to the presheaf U 7→ H i (U, ν ∗ F), where in the last expression U is considered as an element of Xproét .” — Higher direct images as sheafified cohomology presheaves, whose stalks are the colimits of this lemma.

#### Stalks of higher direct images are cohomology of the fibre over the strict localisation (Huber 2.6.1)

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation` · theorem · planet “Stalk formula over strict localisations” · packet H0

Let f: X → Y be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces which is locally of weakly finite type, ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → Y a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank) with strict localisation Y(ξ) = Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit), and F a sheaf of sets (resp. groups, resp. abelian groups or Λ-modules) on X_ét with pullback G to X ×_Y Y(ξ). (a) For n = 0 (resp. n ≤ 1, resp. all n ≥ 0) there is a natural isomorphism (R^n f_*F)_ξ ≅ H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), G), compatible with connecting maps and natural in ξ (in particular equivariant for automorphisms of the strict localisation over y); for K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), (Rf_*K)_ξ ≅ RΓ(X ×_Y Y(ξ), K|). (b) If ξ is the geometric point built from the completion C of an algebraic closure of the completed residue field k(y)^ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (a)), then (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) = (C, C⁺), so (R^n f_*F)_ξ ≅ H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺), F). (c) If y is a point of rank one (a maximal point of the analytic space Y), Y(ξ) = Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is one point and the stalk is the cohomology of the geometric fibre over y (Huber Example 2.6.2). (d) For higher-rank y the fibre over Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) has more points than the fibre over its generic point, and both enter (a). Comparison of the fibre over (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) with the fibre over a larger algebraically closed field (C, C⁺) ⊋ (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is the invariance theorem of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2 (Huber 4.1.1(c)), not part of this node.

**Hypotheses.**

- f quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type (so that X ×_Y V and X ×_Y Y(ξ) exist and are qcqs, locally strongly sheafy over qcqs V).
- ξ a geometric point with C⁺ of any rank; field pairs (C, C⁺) are not replaced by (C, O_C).

**Proof.**

1. (R^n f_*F)_ξ = colim_{N(ξ)^aff} H^n(X ×_Y V, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-of-higher-direct-image-as-colimit).
2. Y(ξ) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} V is a colimit-presented tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit), so its base change X ×_Y Y(ξ) ∼ lim X ×_Y V is a colimit-presented tilde-limit of qcqs spaces (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change (b); quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of X ×_Y V from those of f and of the affinoid V).
3. Replace N(ξ)^aff by its cofinal slice under one neighbourhood (V₀, v̄₀), which has a final object in the sense of the limit, and F by its restriction; apply ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity (its étale-topos hypothesis holds by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit for colimit-presented tilde-limits).
4. Naturality in ξ: a morphism of geometric points transports lifts, hence acts on N(ξ) compatibly with both sides.
5. (b) For the standard geometric point, κ(ξ) is the separable closure of k(y) in C (étale neighbourhoods have finite separable residue extensions, and every finite separable extension is realised by a finite étale neighbourhood, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)); its closure in C is algebraically closed and contains k(y), hence equals the completed algebraic closure C.
6. (c) A rank-one valuation ring has no proper open overrings in its fraction field other than the field, so Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is a point.
7. Complexes: way-out argument on bounded-below complexes using (a) in each degree and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image.

**Acceptance.**

- Finite étale f: the fibre is a finite disjoint union of copies of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), so R^n f_*F = 0 for n > 0 by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/geometric-stalks-at-field-pairs.
- Huber Lemma 3.8.2 (via the decomposition): (R^n g′_* f′_! F′)_y = H^n(X′ ×_{Y′} Y′(y), L) = 0 is an application of (a).
- Bhatt–Hansen, proof of Proposition 3.15: two applications of Huber Example 2.6.2 compute (g^*Rf_*F)_y and (Rf′_*g′^*F)_y at rank-one points y, which is (c).

### Integral, isogeny and rational local systems on preadic spaces

For a prime p and a preadic space X (Kedlaya–Liu §8.2), the integral ℤ_p-local systems are descent data of scheme-theoretic ℤ_p-local systems over affinoid coverings, modulo refinement; the isogeny category rationalises their morphisms; and the rational ℚ_p-local systems are descent data of scheme ℚ_p-local systems. The block proves that an étale cover acquires a finite étale factor near an analytic point, that scheme rational systems acquire local lattices, that adic and étale descent presentations agree, that the two-sided bounded lattices of an integral system form a finite étale space, and that integral local systems on Spec A and on Spã(A, A⁺) are the same.

#### Integral local systems on arbitrary preadic spaces

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/preadic-integral-local-systems` · definition · packet H0

Fix a prime p and a preadic space X in the sense of Kedlaya–Liu §8.2 (Definition 8.2.3). For every preadic affinoid covering U_i = Spã(A_i,A_i⁺), take descent data for finite-free ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A_i): compatible inverse systems T_n of finite locally free ℤ/pⁿ-sheaves, with T_{n+1}/pⁿ ≅ T_n, and transition isomorphisms on affinoid coverings of U_i∩U_j satisfying the triple-overlap cocycle. The category PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem(X) consists of these data modulo common refinement, with morphisms descended on common refinements. It is the category of Definition 8.4.3, without a sheafiness or strong-noetherianness assumption on X. On a locally strongly sheafy analytic space it agrees with the finite-free part of H0/torsion-local-systems; a finitely generated ℤ_p-sheaf with p-torsion is not an integral lattice in this category.

**Construction.**

1. Import the scheme integral-local-system category and its effective étale descent from SF.2.
2. Use the preadic affinoid basis and intersections supplied by R0; take descent categories and identify refinements using D0 stack descent.
3. On the sheafy subcategory use the finite-étale equivalence at every coefficient level, then retain the compatible transition maps.

**API.**

- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem` (structure): The refinement-invariant category described above.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.ofDescent` (constructor): Integral descent data on an affinoid cover give a local system.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction to a preadic open or an affinoid refinement preserves the inverse system and cocycle.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback along a preadic morphism, with canonical identity and composition isomorphisms.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.modPow` (projection): T ↦ T_n is finite locally free over ℤ/pⁿ and T_{n+1}/pⁿ ≅ T_n.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.equivLisse` (compatibility): On strongly sheafy analytic X, equivalence with finite-free lisse ℤ_p-systems in H0.
- `PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem.tensor` (structure): Tensor product, dual and internal Hom, computed levelwise on the T_n over every affinoid; compatible with pullback and with T ↦ T_n; the trivial rank-one system is the unit.

**Unit tests.**

- `preadicZp_constant` (computation): The trivial system of rank r has T_n = (ℤ/pⁿ)^r on every affinoid and identity overlap maps.
- `preadicZp_empty` (degenerate): On the empty preadic space the category has one object and one morphism.
- `preadicZp_lisse` (compatibility): The mod-pⁿ projection on a strongly sheafy analytic X agrees with the corresponding H0 finite-free lisse sheaf.
- `preadicZp_torsion` (non-example): The constant ℤ/p-system is not a rank-one ℤ_p-local system: its next level does not give a free ℤ/p²-lattice.

**Acceptance.**

- Fix a prime p and a preadic space X in the sense of Kedlaya–Liu §8.2 (Definition 8.2.3). For every preadic affinoid covering U_i = Spã(A_i,A_i⁺), take descent data for finite-free ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A_i): compatible inverse systems T_n of finite locally free ℤ/pⁿ-sheaves, with T_{n+1}/pⁿ ≅ T_n, and transition isomorphisms on affinoid coverings of U_i∩U_j satisfying the triple-overlap cocycle. The category PreadicSpace.ZpLocalSystem(X) consists of these data modulo common refinement, with morphisms descended on common refinements. It is the category of Definition 8.4.3, without a sheafiness or strong-noetherianness assumption on X. On a locally strongly sheafy analytic space it agrees with the finite-free part of H0/torsion-local-systems; a finitely generated ℤ_p-sheaf with p-torsion is not an integral lattice in this category.

#### The isogeny category of integral local systems

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/preadic-isogeny-local-systems` · construction · packet H0

For a prime p and preadic X, PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem(X) has the same objects as ZpLocalSystem(X) and Hom(T,T′) = Hom_Zp(T,T′) ⊗_ℤp ℚ_p, with bilinear composition, identity 1⊗id, tensor products and internal Hom induced from integral systems. This is rationalization of a category; it is not its stackification. A rational transition isomorphism and its inverse become integral after multiplication by some powers of p on every quasi-compact overlap where the underlying Hom has descended. The subsequent QpLocalSystem category is obtained by descent, and need not have a global integral lattice.

**Construction.**

1. Rationalize integral morphism modules and their bilinear composition.
2. Use the scheme isogeny category of KL §1.4 on every affinoid and transport its pullbacks.
3. Retain the canonical functor to its stackification, fully faithful on quasi-compact X (one common p-power denominator on a finite cover) and on connected X, rather than asserting effective descent for all covers.

**API.**

- `PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem` (structure): Integral objects with ℚ_p-rationalized morphisms.
- `PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem.rationalize` (constructor): The tensor functor T ↦ T⊗ℚ_p.
- `PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem.hom` (data): Hom is the scalar extension of the integral Hom module, with bilinear composition.
- `PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem.pullback` (functoriality): Rationalization commutes with preadic pullback.
- `PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem.toQp` (compatibility): The canonical faithful functor to QpLocalSystem(X); it is fully faithful when X is quasi-compact or connected, but not in general: on X = ⊔_{n∈ℕ} Spã(K,K°) the endomorphisms of the trivial rank-one system are (∏_n ℤ_p)⊗ℚ_p in the isogeny category and ∏_n ℚ_p in QpLocalSystem(X).

**Unit tests.**

- `isogenyZp_rankOne` (computation): The endomorphisms of the trivial rank-one system on a connected geometric point are ℚ_p.
- `isogenyZp_mulP` (characterisation): Multiplication by p becomes invertible, with inverse p⁻¹, although it is not an integral isomorphism.
- `isogenyZp_zero` (degenerate): The zero system remains zero after rationalization.
- `isogenyZp_notStackification` (non-example): A rational local system with noncompact monodromy on a Tate curve is outside the image of global integral rationalization.

**Acceptance.**

- For a prime p and preadic X, PreadicSpace.IsogenyZpLocalSystem(X) has the same objects as ZpLocalSystem(X) and Hom(T,T′) = Hom_Zp(T,T′) ⊗_ℤp ℚ_p, with bilinear composition, identity 1⊗id, tensor products and internal Hom induced from integral systems. A rational transition isomorphism and its inverse become integral after multiplication by some powers of p on every quasi-compact overlap where the underlying Hom has descended. The subsequent QpLocalSystem category is obtained by descent, and need not have a global integral lattice.

#### Rational local systems by affinoid descent

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/preadic-rational-local-systems` · definition · planet “Rational local systems” · packet H0

For a prime p and arbitrary preadic X, PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem(X) is the category of descent data for scheme étale ℚ_p-local systems V_i on Spec(A_i), over preadic affinoid coverings Spã(A_i,A_i⁺), with restriction isomorphisms on affinoid coverings of intersections, cocycle on triple intersections, and identification under common refinements. Scheme ℚ_p-local systems here mean the étale stackification of the isogeny ℤ_p-local-system category, not arbitrary sheaves of discrete ℚ_p-vector spaces. Tensor product, dual, internal Hom and pullback are obtained by descent. Definition 8.4.3 applies to non-sheafy preadic spaces; comparison with sheaves on A1 sites is restricted to genuine strongly sheafy adic spaces. On affinoid spaces over an analytic field, compare with de Jong’s rational local systems through H0/analytic-rational-representation-equivalence.

**Construction.**

1. Import scheme ℚ_p-local systems as an étale stack, including refinement equivalences, from SF.2.
2. Apply KL Definition 8.4.3 to the affinoid basis of a preadic space.
3. Glue morphisms and tensor structures on common refinements; the restriction functors inherit identity and composition coherence.

**API.**

- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem` (structure): The category of rational local systems by affinoid descent.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.ofDescent` (constructor): Objects and cocycles on an affinoid cover define a rational local system.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.refine` (equivalence): Common refinement induces an equivalence of the descent presentations.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.pullback` (functoriality): Pullback preserves tensor products and duals, with coherent identity and composition maps.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.rank` (projection): The finite rank is locally constant, determined by the affinoid scheme local systems.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.rationalize` (constructor): An integral local system gives a rational local system by scalar extension.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.homDescent` (extensionality): Morphisms are equal if their restrictions agree on a covering.
- `PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem.tensor` (structure): Tensor product, dual and internal Hom obtained by descent from Spec(A_i), with unit the trivial rank-one system; rationalize and pullback are tensor functors.

**Unit tests.**

- `preadicQp_field` (compatibility): On Spã(K,K⁺) for a complete field, the category agrees with continuous finite-dimensional ℚ_p-representations of Gal(K^sep/K).
- `preadicQp_zero` (degenerate): Rank zero is the zero object, preserved by every pullback.
- `preadicQp_refinement` (characterisation): Refining every affinoid of a trivial rank-one descent datum gives an isomorphic object with identity transitions.
- `preadicQp_noncompact` (non-example): The rank-one rational local system on a Tate curve with generator acting by p has no global integral lattice.

**Acceptance.**

- For a prime p and arbitrary preadic X, PreadicSpace.QpLocalSystem(X) is the category of descent data for scheme étale ℚ_p-local systems V_i on Spec(A_i), over preadic affinoid coverings Spã(A_i,A_i⁺), with restriction isomorphisms on affinoid coverings of intersections, cocycle on triple intersections, and identification under common refinements. Scheme ℚ_p-local systems here mean the étale stackification of the isogeny ℤ_p-local-system category, not arbitrary sheaves of discrete ℚ_p-vector spaces. Tensor product, dual, internal Hom and pullback are obtained by descent. Definition 8.4.3 applies to non-sheafy preadic spaces; comparison with sheaves on A1 sites is restricted to genuine strongly sheafy adic spaces. On affinoid spaces over an analytic field, compare with de Jong’s rational local systems through H0/analytic-rational-representation-equivalence.

**Used by.**

- Kedlaya–Liu §8.4; PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: Rational local systems and integral lattices are the input to period-sheaf coefficients, before any period comparison.

**Depends on.** `H0/preadic-integral-local-systems`, `H0/preadic-isogeny-local-systems`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-analytic-tate-local`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions`.

**Library target.** module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Cohomology/LocalSystem`, namespace `TauCeti.PreadicSpace`.

**Sources.**

- [KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015], Definition 8.4.3, p. 168: “specify a local system Vi over Spec(Ai) for each i, then cover each intersection Ui ∩ Uj with preadic affinoid spaces Spã(Bk, Bk+) and define isomorphisms of the restrictions of Vi and Vj to Bk satisfying the cocycle condition.” — The source specifies affinoid descent for both integral and rational local systems.

#### A finite étale factor near an analytic point

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-cover-finite-factor-near-analytic-point` · lemma · packet H0

Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and Spec(A′)→Spec(A) a surjective étale morphism. For every α∈M(A) there is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α for which A′⊗_A B decomposes as a finite product of rings, with at least one factor faithfully finite étale over B. Encircling is the neighborhood notion of KL §2.4; replacing it by an arbitrary rational subset containing α loses the neighborhood assertion. The algebra A′⊗_A B is the algebraic base change of the scheme cover, not an unspecified completion.

**Proof.**

1. Choose a prime of A′ over the support prime of α and extend the norm to its residue field.
2. Apply the local Jacobian criterion and KL 2.4.17 to obtain a rational neighborhood on which the étale component has an invertible Jacobian.
3. Separate the component and use the point lying above α to retain a faithfully finite étale factor, as in KL 8.4.1.

**Acceptance.**

- For a faithfully finite étale A′/A, choose the identity localization and the whole A′ as the factor.
- A non-surjective open immersion need not supply a faithful factor near a point outside its image.

**Depends on.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0/spectrum`.

**Library target.** module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Cohomology/LocalSystem`, namespace `TauCeti.AdicSpace`.

**Sources.**

- [KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015], Lemma 8.4.1 and proof, p. 167: “Then for any α ∈ M(A), there exists a rational localization (A, A+) → (B, B+) encircling α such that A′ ⊗A B splits as a direct sum of subrings, at least one of which is faithfully finite étale over B.” — The finite factor is obtained near every analytic point.

#### A scheme rational local system acquires a local lattice

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/scheme-rational-local-lattice` · lemma · packet H0

Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring, V a scheme étale ℚ_p-local system on Spec(A), and α∈M(A). There is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α such that V|_Spec(B) is isomorphic to T⊗ℚ_p for an integral ℤ_p-local system T on Spec(B).

**Proof.**

1. Present V étale-locally by isogeny integral systems using scheme stackification.
2. Apply the finite-factor lemma near α.
3. Apply effective descent of isogeny local systems along a faithfully finite étale ring map (KL Lemma 1.4.8), imported from SF.2.

**Acceptance.**

- Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring, V a scheme étale ℚ_p-local system on Spec(A), and α∈M(A). There is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α such that V|_Spec(B) is isomorphic to T⊗ℚ_p for an integral ℤ_p-local system T on Spec(B).

Then for any α ∈ M(A), there exists a rational localization (A, A+) → (B, B+) encircling α such that V ×Spec(A) Spec(B) is an isogeny Zp-local system on Spec(B).” — The proof uses Lemma 1.4.8 and Lemma 8.4.1.

#### Adic and étale presentations of preadic local systems

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/preadic-local-system-etale-descent` · comparison · packet H0

The integral and rational local-system categories of KL Definition 8.4.3 are unchanged if preadic étale covering families replace the adic open covering families in the descent presentation. The comparison functors preserve pullback, rank, tensor product and dual; on strongly sheafy spaces they agree with the corresponding local-system categories on A1’s ordinary étale site. The assertion extends the local-system categories, not every torsion cohomology theorem of H0, to arbitrary preadic spaces.

**Proof.**

1. Use local factorization of preadic étale maps into a rational localization and a finite étale map, supplied by A1.
2. Descend integral systems along finite étale maps and rational systems along their stack descent.
3. Compare on common refinements to construct inverse equivalences, as KL Remark 8.4.4.

**Acceptance.**

- The integral and rational local-system categories of KL Definition 8.4.3 are unchanged if preadic étale covering families replace the adic open covering families in the descent presentation. The comparison functors preserve pullback, rank, tensor product and dual; on strongly sheafy spaces they agree with the corresponding local-system categories on A1’s ordinary étale site. The assertion extends the local-system categories, not every torsion cohomology theorem of H0, to arbitrary preadic spaces.

**Library target.** module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Cohomology/LocalSystem`, namespace `TauCeti.AdicSpace`.

**Sources.**

- [KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015], Remark 8.4.4, p. 168: “Thanks to the local factorization of étale morphisms, one gets the same categories of local systems if one takes coverings in the étale topology rather than the adic topology.” — Local factorization makes the two kinds of covering presentation equivalent.

#### Bounded lattices in an integral local system

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/bounded-lattices-in-preadic-local-systems` · construction · packet H0

For an integral ℤ_p-local system T on a preadic X and m≥0, define L_m(T)(Y) to be isomorphism classes of pairs (T′,ι), with T′ integral on Y and ι:T_Y⊗ℚ_p ≅ T′⊗ℚ_p satisfying p^mι∈Hom(T_Y,T′) and p^mι⁻¹∈Hom(T′,T_Y). It is represented by a finite étale preadic X-space. At a geometric point it is the finite set of lattices between p^m T_x and p^(−m)T_x; the two inequalities are both required. It has an inclusion relation represented by a finite étale subspace of L_m(T)×_X L_m(T) and a canonical operation taking the sum of finitely many bounded lattices. These are the analytic transports of KL Remark 1.4.7, used in Proposition 8.4.6.

**Construction.**

1. Import the finite étale bounded-lattice scheme L_m(T), its inclusion relation and finite sums from SF.2 (KL Remark 1.4.7).
2. Apply the finite-étale algebra/space correspondence of A1 on each affinoid.
3. Glue along overlaps; base change of the finite mod-p-power lattice data gives representability without a sheafiness assumption on X.

**API.**

- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice` (structure): The moduli functor with bounds on ι and ι⁻¹.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.finiteEtale` (structure): L_m(T) is finite étale over X.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.pullback` (functoriality): L_m(T_Y) ≅ L_m(T)×_X Y.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.inclusion` (relation): The finite étale relation detects whether the rationally identified lattices are included.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.sup` (constructor): Finite lattice sums are canonical and compatible with base change.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore` (structure): For submodules T,T′ of a ℚ_p-vector space with compatible ℤ_p scalar restriction, the geometric-fibre core is the conjunction p^mT⊆T′ and p^mT′⊆T. It records both bounds, without asserting finite freeness or representability.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore.zero_iff` (characterisation): At m=0 the two-sided bound is equivalent to T=T′.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore.refl` (constructor): Every submodule is two-sided bounded relative to itself at every nonnegative m.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore.symm` (relation): The two-sided bound is symmetric in T,T′.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore.trans` (relation): Bounds m and n compose to a bound m+n.
- `PreadicSpace.BoundedLattice.FiberCore.mono` (relation): Increasing m preserves the two-sided bound.

**Unit tests.**

- `boundedLattice_zeroBound` (computation): L_0(T) has one point on each geometric fibre: the original lattice.
- `boundedLattice_zeroRank` (degenerate): For T=0, L_m(T) is the terminal X-space for every m.
- `boundedLattice_rankOne` (computation): For trivial rank one over a geometric point, L_m has 2m+1 points, the lattices p^aℤ_p with −m≤a≤m.
- `boundedLattice_oneSided` (non-example): The condition p^mι integral alone admits arbitrarily large lattices; it does not define the finite L_m.
- `boundedLatticeCore_zero` (computation): At bound zero the two-sided core identifies T and T′.
- `boundedLatticeCore_zeroRank` (degenerate): The zero submodule is two-sided bounded with itself at every m.
- `boundedLatticeCore_composition` (compatibility): Two successive bounds add, so a bound m and a bound n give m+n.

**Acceptance.**

- For an integral ℤ_p-local system T on a preadic X and m≥0, define L_m(T)(Y) to be isomorphism classes of pairs (T′,ι), with T′ integral on Y and ι:T_Y⊗ℚ_p ≅ T′⊗ℚ_p satisfying p^mι∈Hom(T_Y,T′) and p^mι⁻¹∈Hom(T′,T_Y). It is represented by a finite étale preadic X-space. At a geometric point it is the finite set of lattices between p^m T_x and p^(−m)T_x; the two inequalities are both required. It has an inclusion relation represented by a finite étale subspace of L_m(T)×_X L_m(T) and a canonical operation taking the sum of finitely many bounded lattices. These are the analytic transports of KL Remark 1.4.7, used in Proposition 8.4.6.

**Used by.**

- Kedlaya–Liu §8.4; PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational: Rational local systems and integral lattices are the input to period-sheaf coefficients, before any period comparison.

#### Integral local systems agree on Spec and preadic Spa

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/integral-spec-preadic-equivalence` · comparison · packet H0

For every adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℤ_p-Loc(Spec A)→ZpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is an equivalence, and induces an equivalence on the isogeny categories. Its mod-pⁿ functors are the finite-étale algebra/space comparisons of A1. This does not assert an equivalence of the full étale topoi or an equivalence of their rational stackifications.

**Proof.**

1. Integral local systems are determined by compatible finite étale covers at every coefficient level (KL Remark 1.4.3).
2. Apply effective rational-localization descent of finite étale algebras (KL Theorem 2.6.9), requested from R0/A1.
3. Glue the compatible coefficient transitions, then rationalize morphisms.

**Acceptance.**

- For every adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℤ_p-Loc(Spec A)→ZpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is an equivalence, and induces an equivalence on the isogeny categories. Its mod-pⁿ functors are the finite-étale algebra/space comparisons of A1. This does not assert an equivalence of the full étale topoi or an equivalence of their rational stackifications.

### De Jong's analytic coverings and the analytic fundamental group

De Jong's analytic étale covering spaces of a Berkovich space: separatedness, base change, images, effective étale descent and componentwise quotients; the fibre functor at a geometric point; the comparison of topological coverings with coverings of |X|; the analytic fundamental group π₁^an(X, x) = Aut(F_x) with its stabiliser topology, which is Hausdorff and prodiscrete but need not be profinite; paths between fibre functors; the duality between coverings (enlarged by arbitrary disjoint unions) and continuous discrete π₁^an-sets; and π₁^alg as the profinite completion of π₁^an, with dense image but not surjective (de Jong Remark 2.11(i)).

#### De Jong étale covering spaces

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-etale-covering-spaces` · definition · packet H0

For a k-analytic Berkovich space X, an analytic étale covering map f:Y→X means that every x∈X has an ordinary open neighborhood U such that f⁻¹(U) is a disjoint union of spaces finite étale over U. A topological covering is the case where these finite étale pieces are isomorphisms. Cov_X is the category of these maps over X, including the empty map; it is not the category of all étale maps and is not silently enlarged to arbitrary disjoint unions. On Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces, transport this definition to the corresponding taut adic spaces via Huber’s equivalence with Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces (requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0). For a quasi-separated rigid space X, de Jong §5 requires, when X is affinoid, that Y be paracompact and that every analytic point have a wide affinoid neighbourhood U with Y×_X U a disjoint union of affinoids finite étale over U, and in general that every base change to an affinoid X′ be such a covering; for X coming from a Hausdorff strictly k-analytic space this agrees with Definition 2.1. The weaker condition over an admissible affinoid covering (de Jong’s almost étale covering maps) is not used.

**Construction.**

1. Use the Berkovich carrier and its comparison with taut adic spaces (TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0) and A1’s finite étale morphisms.
2. Define the local finite-étale condition on ordinary open neighborhoods.
3. Transport the rigid version along the equivalence, retaining its neighborhood qualification.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover` (structure): The local disjoint-finite-étale condition and its category.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.ofFiniteEtale` (constructor): Every finite étale map is an analytic covering.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.ofTopological` (constructor): A topological covering with its canonical analytic structure is an analytic covering.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.pullback` (functoriality): Coverings are stable under arbitrary analytic base change.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.finiteCoproduct` (structure): Finite coproducts, including the empty covering, stay in Cov_X.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.berkovichEquiv` (compatibility): Agreement with de Jong Definition 2.1 on Hausdorff strictly analytic spaces.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.fiberProduct` (structure): For coverings Y₁,Y₂ of X, Y₁×_X Y₂ is a covering of X (de Jong p. 91).
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleCover.ofMorphism` (relation): A morphism g:Y₁→Y₂ of coverings of X is itself an étale covering map; compositions of covering maps need not be coverings (de Jong p. 91).

**Unit tests.**

- `analyticCover_identity` (degenerate): The identity and empty map are covering spaces.
- `analyticCover_finite` (compatibility): A finite étale covering has the same fibres as A1’s finite étale space.
- `analyticCover_open` (non-example): The open immersion of a nonempty proper open subset of connected X is not an analytic covering: its image is not a union of connected components.

**Acceptance.**

- For a k-analytic Berkovich space X, an analytic étale covering map f:Y→X means that every x∈X has an ordinary open neighborhood U such that f⁻¹(U) is a disjoint union of spaces finite étale over U. A topological covering is the case where these finite étale pieces are isomorphisms. Cov_X is the category of these maps over X, including the empty map; it is not the category of all étale maps and is not silently enlarged to arbitrary disjoint unions. On Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces, transport this definition to the corresponding taut adic spaces via Huber’s equivalence with Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces (requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0). For a quasi-separated rigid space X, de Jong §5 requires, when X is affinoid, that Y be paracompact and that every analytic point have a wide affinoid neighbourhood U with Y×_X U a disjoint union of affinoids finite étale over U, and in general that every base change to an affinoid X′ be such a covering; for X coming from a Hausdorff strictly k-analytic space this agrees with Definition 2.1. The weaker condition over an admissible affinoid covering (de Jong’s almost étale covering maps) is not used.

**Used by.**

- de Jong Theorems 2.10 and 4.2; KL Definition 8.4.3 and Remark 8.4.8: The covering category defines the analytic fibre functor and allows noncompact rational monodromy.

**Depends on.** `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`.

**Library target.** module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Cohomology/LocalSystem`, namespace `TauCeti.AdicSpace`.

**Sources.**

- [deJong-AnalyticFundamentalGroups-1995], Definition 2.1, p. 91; §5, p. 106: “We say that Y is an étale covering space of X or that f is an étale covering map if for all x ∈ X there exists an open neighbourhood U ⊂ X of x such that f−1(U) is a disjoint union of spaces Vi, each mapping finite étale to U.” — Coverings are locally disjoint unions of finite étale maps in the Berkovich topology.
- [deJong-AnalyticFundamentalGroups-1995], §5, p. 106: “If X is affinoid, we demand that Y be paracompact and that the associated morphism of Berkovich spaces (see [B2, 1.6.1]) is an étale covering space.” — The rigid-analytic version carries a paracompactness condition.

#### Analytic covering maps are separated

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-separatedness` · lemma · packet H0

A de Jong étale covering Y→X is separated. On an ordinary neighbourhood where it is a disjoint union of finite étale spaces, each diagonal is closed and the disjoint-component diagonal is closed; separatedness then descends over the open covering of X.

**Proof.**

1. Reduce to the local disjoint finite-étale presentation.
2. Check the diagonal on each pair of components and use the local criterion for separatedness.

**Acceptance.**

- A de Jong étale covering Y→X is separated. On an ordinary neighbourhood where it is a disjoint union of finite étale spaces, each diagonal is closed and the disjoint-component diagonal is closed; separatedness then descends over the open covering of X.

#### Base change of analytic coverings

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-base-change` · lemma · packet H0

For an arbitrary analytic map X′→X and a de Jong covering Y→X, Y×_X X′→X′ is again a covering. Pull back the ordinary neighbourhoods and their disjoint finite-étale presentations; base change of each finite étale piece is finite étale.

**Proof.**

1. Pull back a neighbourhood presentation around the image of a point of X′.
2. Use finite-étale base change on every piece; their disjoint union is the full preimage.

**Acceptance.**

- For an arbitrary analytic map X′→X and a de Jong covering Y→X, Y×_X X′→X′ is again a covering. Pull back the ordinary neighbourhoods and their disjoint finite-étale presentations; base change of each finite étale piece is finite étale.

#### Images of analytic coverings are unions of components

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-image-components` · lemma · packet H0

The image of a de Jong covering Y→X is a union of connected components of X. In particular, on connected X any nonempty covering is surjective. This follows from the locally constant image condition of finite étale pieces, with the uniform ordinary neighbourhood in the covering definition.

**Proof.**

1. On a connected small neighbourhood each nonempty finite étale component is surjective.
2. The image and its complement are locally open; propagate along connected components.

**Acceptance.**

- The image of a de Jong covering Y→X is a union of connected components of X. In particular, on connected X any nonempty covering is surjective. This follows from the locally constant image condition of finite étale pieces, with the uniform ordinary neighbourhood in the covering definition.

#### Representability of analytic coverings is étale local

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-effective-etale-descent` · theorem · packet H0

An étale sheaf on X_et is represented by a de Jong covering if and only if its pullback to each member of an étale covering of X is so. Effective descent retains a single ordinary neighbourhood on which all fibres are a disjoint union of finite étale pieces; arbitrary sheaf representability alone would not prove this covering condition.

**Proof.**

1. Reduce the descent map locally to a finite étale Galois covering.
2. For each component take its finite orbit under the finite descent group.
3. Descend those finite étale unions and glue them over ordinary neighbourhoods, as de Jong Lemma 2.3.

**Acceptance.**

- An étale sheaf on X_et is represented by a de Jong covering if and only if its pullback to each member of an étale covering of X is so. Effective descent retains a single ordinary neighbourhood on which all fibres are a disjoint union of finite étale pieces; arbitrary sheaf representability alone would not prove this covering condition.

The sheaf F is representable by an étale covering space of X if and only if F|Ui is representable by an étale covering space of Ui for each i.” — Local covering geometry, orbit quotients and the lattice-cover construction.

#### Componentwise equivalence-relation quotients of coverings

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-componentwise-quotient` · theorem · packet H0

For a de Jong covering Y→X and an equivalence relation R which is a union of connected components of Y×_X Y, the étale quotient sheaf Y/R is represented by a de Jong covering. Locally reduce to finite étale pieces and quotient by the descended relation; the component condition is essential to that reduction.

**Proof.**

1. After finite étale base change split the local finite pieces.
2. The componentwise relation descends to a relation on the discrete pieces.
3. Construct their quotients and apply effective étale descent, as de Jong Lemma 2.4.

#### Étale descent and quotients for analytic coverings

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-descent-and-quotients` · theorem · packet H0

A sheaf of sets on X_ét is representable by a de Jong covering iff it is so after an étale covering of X. If Y→X is such a covering and R⊆Y×_X Y is an equivalence relation that is a union of connected components, then the quotient étale sheaf Y/R is representable by a de Jong covering. Coverings are separated and stable under base change; their images are unions of connected components. The quotient assertion retains the connected-component condition on R.

**Proof.**

1. Étale-locally reduce to a finite Galois covering of a neighborhood.
2. A finite group preserves finite unions of the covering components, so scheme finite-étale descent constructs the local quotients.
3. Glue the local representing spaces; use the same local finite-étale reduction for R, as de Jong Lemmas 2.2–2.4.

**Acceptance.**

- A sheaf of sets on X_ét is representable by a de Jong covering iff it is so after an étale covering of X. If Y→X is such a covering and R⊆Y×_X Y is an equivalence relation that is a union of connected components, then the quotient étale sheaf Y/R is representable by a de Jong covering. Coverings are separated and stable under base change; their images are unions of connected components. The quotient assertion retains the connected-component condition on R.

#### The fibre functor on analytic coverings

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-fiber-functor` · construction · packet H0

For a geometric point x:M(K)→X with K algebraically closed complete, define F_x:Cov_X→Set by F_x(Y)=Y×_X M(K), viewed as its discrete set of K-points. Morphisms act by the induced maps on fibres. The functor preserves finite fibre products and existing disjoint unions. Its restrictions to finite étale and topological coverings define the algebraic and topological fibre functors. The same fibre functor on the corresponding taut adic space uses Spa(K,O_K); it agrees with A1’s geometric stalk on a represented covering.

**Construction.**

1. Use the splitting of finite étale spaces over an algebraically closed field on each local component.
2. Take the resulting discrete fibre and induced maps.
3. Identify the represented sheaf stalk with this fibre through A1 and R1.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.AnalyticCoverFiber` (constructor): The fibre functor F_x on Cov_X.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticCoverFiber.map` (functoriality): Maps of coverings induce fibre maps respecting identity and composition.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticCoverFiber.pullback` (compatibility): A pointed analytic map identifies the fibre of a pulled-back covering.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticCoverFiber.stalk` (equivalence): F_x(Y) is the A1 geometric stalk of the represented covering sheaf.

**Unit tests.**

- `analyticFiber_identity` (computation): The identity covering has a singleton fibre.
- `analyticFiber_empty` (degenerate): The empty covering has the empty fibre.
- `analyticFiber_field` (compatibility): For X=M(k) and Y=M(L), L/k finite separable, the fibre is Hom_k(L,K).

**Acceptance.**

#### Analytic and underlying topological coverings

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-topological-covering-equivalence` · comparison · packet H0

The category of topological analytic covering spaces of a k-analytic X is equivalent to the category of topological covering spaces of |X|. A topological covering T→|X| defines the étale sheaf U↦Hom_|X|(|U|,T); étale-local covering representability equips T with its unique analytic covering structure. Thus π₁^top depends only on (|X|,x), as required by the Tate-curve monodromy example.

**Proof.**

1. Construct the sheaf of continuous lifts to the underlying covering.
2. Apply de Jong Lemma 2.3 locally, then glue the represented analytic covering.
3. Check that taking underlying spaces and this construction are inverse.

- The category of topological analytic covering spaces of a k-analytic X is equivalent to the category of topological covering spaces of |X|. A topological covering T→|X| defines the étale sheaf U↦Hom_|X|(|U|,T); étale-local covering representability equips T with its unique analytic covering structure. Thus π₁^top depends only on (|X|,x), as required by the Tate-curve monodromy example.

#### De Jong analytic étale fundamental group

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-etale-fundamental-group` · definition · planet “Étale fundamental group of an analytic space” · packet H0

For a connected k-analytic space X with geometric point x, define π₁^an(X,x)=Aut(F_x), where F_x is the fibre functor on de Jong covering spaces. Give it the topology whose identity neighborhoods are stabilizers H(Y,y) of y∈F_x(Y), Y∈Cov_X; finite intersections and conjugates again occur. This topological group need not be profinite. Restriction to finite étale coverings gives a continuous map to the profinite algebraic fundamental group π₁^alg; restriction to topological coverings gives the topological covering group. On taut strictly analytic adic spaces this is the transported analytic group. Scheme IG.0 is not a supplier for this definition.

**Construction.**

1. Define automorphisms of the fibre functor and point stabilizers.
2. Finite fibre products and the identity γH(Y,y)γ⁻¹=H(Y,γy) give a subgroup neighborhood basis.
3. Use restriction of natural automorphisms for the algebraic and topological comparison maps.

**API.**

- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup` (structure): Aut(F_x) with the stabilizer topology.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup.action` (data): The continuous action on every discrete covering fibre.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup.stabilizerBasis` (characterisation): H(Y,y) is a neighborhood basis at the identity.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup.map` (functoriality): Pointed analytic maps give continuous homomorphisms with identity and composition laws.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup.toAlgebraic` (compatibility): Restriction to finite coverings is the algebraic profinite comparison.
- `AdicSpace.AnalyticEtaleFundamentalGroup.toTopological` (compatibility): Restriction to topological coverings is the topological comparison.

- `analyticPi_field` (compatibility): For X=M(k), π₁^an is Gal(k^sep/k) with its profinite topology.
- `analyticPi_geometricPoint` (degenerate): For X=M(C), C algebraically closed, π₁^an is trivial.
- `analyticPi_nonProfinite` (non-example): For a Tate elliptic curve the topological quotient is ℤ; π₁^an cannot be replaced by its profinite finite-cover quotient.

#### Prodiscreteness of the analytic fundamental group

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-fundamental-group-prodiscreteness` · theorem · packet H0

For π=π₁^an(X,x), the natural map π→lim_H π/H, over the point-stabilizer neighborhood system with quotient maps, is a homeomorphism of spaces. Thus π is Hausdorff and prodiscrete in de Jong’s sense. The stabilizers need not be normal and this formula is not a presentation as an inverse limit of finite groups.

**Proof.**

1. A compatible system of cosets acts consistently on each covering fibre.
2. The resulting permutations commute with all covering morphisms and hence define an element of Aut(F_x).
3. Stabilizer neighborhoods identify the topology (de Jong Lemma 2.7).

**Acceptance.**

- For π=π₁^an(X,x), the natural map π→lim_H π/H, over the point-stabilizer neighborhood system with quotient maps, is a homeomorphism of spaces. Thus π is Hausdorff and prodiscrete in de Jong’s sense. The stabilizers need not be normal and this formula is not a presentation as an inverse limit of finite groups.

#### Paths between analytic fibre functors

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-paths` · theorem · packet H0

For a connected k-analytic Berkovich X and any geometric points x,x′, there exists a natural isomorphism F_x≅F_x′ on de Jong covering spaces. A choice induces a continuous isomorphism of analytic fundamental groups, unique up to inner conjugation; no canonical path is asserted.

**Proof.**

1. Reduce to connected affinoid neighborhoods and use arcwise connectedness supplied by R1’s Berkovich geometry.
2. For each finite open covering along an arc, compose paths in finite étale Galois categories on successive overlaps.
3. The possible compositions form nonempty compact sets compatible under refinement; their inverse limit supplies the natural isomorphism (de Jong Theorem 2.9).

**Acceptance.**

- For a connected k-analytic Berkovich X and any geometric points x,x′, there exists a natural isomorphism F_x≅F_x′ on de Jong covering spaces. A choice induces a continuous isomorphism of analytic fundamental groups, unique up to inner conjugation; no canonical path is asserted.

#### Connected coverings and fibre orbits

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-connected-orbits` · lemma · packet H0

For connected X, the fibres of connected components of a de Jong covering are exactly the π₁^an-orbits in F_x(Y). Connected coverings therefore have transitive fibre action and, X being connected, are surjective onto X. This is the connected-component/orbit step in the proof of de Jong 2.10.

**Proof.**

1. Use path transport to identify the points over different base points in a connected covering component.
2. Use fibre-functor automorphisms to identify the orbit over the fixed base point.
3. Apply the component image lemma for surjectivity.

**Acceptance.**

- For connected X, the fibres of connected components of a de Jong covering are exactly the π₁^an-orbits in F_x(Y). Connected coverings therefore have transitive fibre action and, X being connected, are surjective onto X. This is the connected-component/orbit step in the proof of de Jong 2.10.

#### Realization of a transitive open-stabilizer action

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-open-stabilizer-realization` · theorem · packet H0

For π=π₁^an(X,x) and an open subgroup H⊆π, the continuous transitive discrete action π/H is represented by a connected de Jong covering. #### Duality for analytic coverings and continuous actions

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-covering-duality` · theorem · packet H0

For connected X with geometric point x, F_x:Cov_X→π₁^an(X,x)-Set is fully faithful and every transitive continuous discrete action occurs. The category of arbitrary disjoint unions of objects of Cov_X is equivalent to all continuous discrete π₁^an-sets. The original Cov_X itself is not asserted equivalent to all such sets: arbitrary disjoint unions need not satisfy the uniform local covering condition. Restriction to finite étale covers is an equivalence with finite continuous π₁^alg-sets.

**Proof.**

1. Paths identify connected components of a covering with group orbits on its fibre.
2. Morphisms are recovered from componentwise graphs in fibre products, giving full faithfulness.
3. For an open stabilizer construct the desired transitive orbit by quotienting a covering by a union of components, then take formal disjoint unions (de Jong Theorem 2.10(i)).

**Acceptance.**

- The regular action of the discrete deck group of a connected topological Galois cover recovers that cover.
- Finite covering fibres agree with the ordinary finite-étale Galois category.

Thus the category π1(X, x̄)-Sets is naturally equivalent to the category of disjoint unions of étale covering spaces of X.” — The theorem distinguishes Cov_X from its disjoint-union enlargement.

#### π₁^alg as the profinite completion of analytic monodromy

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-fundamental-group-profinite-quotient` · theorem · packet H0

The algebraic group π₁^alg(X,x) is profinite. Every continuous homomorphism π₁^an(X,x)→G to a profinite group factors uniquely through π₁^alg(X,x), and the canonical maps to π₁^alg and π₁^top have dense image. The map to π₁^alg is not surjective in general: for two projective lines over an algebraically closed field glued at 0 and ∞, π₁^alg = ℤ̂ and the map factors through ℤ ⊂ ℤ̂ (de Jong Remark 2.11(i)). A continuous representation on a finite-free ℤ_p-module factors through π₁^alg, since GL_r(ℤ_p) is profinite; a representation on ℚ_p may have noncompact image and need not do so.

**Proof.**

1. Use finite covering duality for each finite quotient of G and pass to the profinite limit.
2. The fully faithful inclusions of finite and topological covering categories give density (de Jong Theorem 2.10(iii)–(iv)).
3. Apply the universal property to GL_r(ℤ_p), importing its profinite structure from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1.

**Acceptance.**

The map to π₁^alg is not surjective in general: for two projective lines over an algebraically closed field glued at 0 and ∞, π₁^alg = ℤ̂ and the map factors through ℤ ⊂ ℤ̂ (de Jong Remark 2.11(i)). A continuous representation on a finite-free ℤ_p-module factors through π₁^alg, since GL_r(ℤ_p) is profinite; a representation on ℚ_p may have noncompact image and need not do so.

### Lattices and rational descent

The étale sheaf of integral lattices in a rational local system is represented by a de Jong covering, bounded lattice strata are controlled by finite quotients, and every rational local system on an adic Banach ring is locally an isogeny ℤ_p-local system and admits a descent presentation by isogeny systems on a strong rational covering.

#### The analytic covering of integral lattices

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-rational-lattice-cover` · construction · packet H0

For an étale ℚ_p-local system V on a k-analytic X, let Lat(V) be the étale sheaf whose sections are finite-free integral ℤ_p-lattices in V, with inclusion after rationalization equal to V. It is represented by a de Jong covering: locally choose an integral presentation T, and express its lattice sheaf as the increasing union of the open and closed finite étale subspaces L_m(T), hence as the disjoint union of the finite étale differences L_m(T)∖L_{m−1}(T). Étale-local representability then gives a global analytic covering. This construction allows Lat(V) to lack a global section.

**Construction.**

1. Use local integral presentations of the rational system.
2. Decompose lattices by the least m with p^mT⊆T′⊆p^(−m)T; the strata L_m(T)∖L_{m−1}(T) are open, closed and finite étale.
3. Apply effective descent for analytic coverings.

**API.**

- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover` (structure): The represented covering Lat(V)→X.
- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover.fiber` (projection): At x its points are ℤ_p-lattices in the rational fibre V_x.
- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover.boundedStratum` (constructor): For a local integral presentation T, the finite étale stratum L_m(T)∖L_{m−1}(T) of lattices with least two-sided bound m; Lat(V) is locally the disjoint union of these strata.
- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover.universalLattice` (data): The tautological integral system on Lat(V) rationalizes to the pullback of V.
- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover.pullback` (functoriality): Lat(f^*V)≅Lat(V)×_X X′.
- `AnalyticRationalLatticeCover.section` (characterisation): Global sections correspond to global integral lattices in V.

**Unit tests.**

- `latticeCover_rankZero` (degenerate): For V=0 the lattice cover is X with its unique zero lattice.
- `latticeCover_rankOnePoint` (computation): For trivial rank-one V at a geometric point, the lattice set is {p^aℤ_p | a∈ℤ}.
- `latticeCover_noncompact` (non-example): The Tate-curve p^ℤ monodromy system has no section of its lattice cover.

**Acceptance.**

- For an étale ℚ_p-local system V on a k-analytic X, let Lat(V) be the étale sheaf whose sections are finite-free integral ℤ_p-lattices in V, with inclusion after rationalization equal to V. It is represented by a de Jong covering: locally choose an integral presentation T, and express its lattice sheaf as the increasing union of the open and closed finite étale subspaces L_m(T), hence as the disjoint union of the finite étale differences L_m(T)∖L_{m−1}(T). Étale-local representability then gives a global analytic covering. This construction allows Lat(V) to lack a global section.

**Used by.**

- de Jong Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.4: The tautological lattice proves the representation equivalence and ordinary-open local lattices.

#### Bounded lattice strata are controlled by finite quotients

`ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/analytic-bounded-lattice-finite-quotient` · lemma · packet H0

For an integral system T and m≥0, a lattice T′ with p^mT⊆T′⊆p^(−m)T is determined by the submodule T′/p^mT of the finite locally free quotient p^(−m)T/p^mT. The freeness and lattice conditions select a finite locally constant subset of the finite submodule set. Thus the two-sided bounded-lattice stratum is finite étale locally and globally represented by the corresponding finite étale preadic space.

**Proof.**

1. Recover T′ as the preimage of its quotient submodule.
2. Check lattice/freeness after an integral trivializing cover.
3. Use the finite-étale algebra/space correspondence and integral descent.

**Acceptance.**

- For an integral system T and m≥0, a lattice T′ with p^mT⊆T′⊆p^(−m)T is determined by the submodule T′/p^mT of the finite locally free quotient p^(−m)T/p^mT. The freeness and lattice conditions select a finite locally constant subset of the finite submodule set. Thus the two-sided bounded-lattice stratum is finite étale locally and globally represented by the corresponding finite étale preadic space.
